notes: [round 1] Plan: construct a domain-stratified, uniformly weighted 100-item free-response knowledge test. Initial target coverage: Science and technology 16, Politics 12, Geography 12, History 10, Art 10, Music 10, Sports 10, Other 8, TV shows 6, Video games 6. This balances broad scientific/civic/world knowledge against cultural domains without simply reproducing the pool's acquisition skew. Review full questions and fixed keys before retention; exclude underspecified dates, unstable present-tense facts, disputed premises, and answers with especially brittle exact-match formatting. Panel results will diagnose floor/ceiling and differentiation, not serve as the sole selection criterion. No model-specific optimization is intended. Four rounds: establish reviewed draft; diagnose and replace; refine validity and coverage; final audit and submit.

[round 1] Round 1 content review: inspected 100 retained questions and keys plus alternatives across early, middle and late pool positions. Rejected EMB 110 sole-designer wording (team/attribution ambiguity), unsupported last-18th-century-president key (F1633; Fillmore was born in 1800), Seiko/Grand Seiko branding ambiguity, and multiple fixed keys requiring incidental terminal punctuation, honorifics or unusually long names. Six wording edits clarify collision energy, Kashmir Line of Control, Olympic fencing competition, Game of Thrones continuity, Bernini commission, and Wrinch's scientific contribution. Initial draft preserves the planned 10-domain quotas. Exact matching remains a limitation: names/transliterations and titles can have valid aliases; select against particularly brittle keys rather than modifying fixed keys. No independent source-browsing tool is available; human-verified pool provenance is relied on, with internal consistency and factual plausibility checks rather than a claim of fresh citation verification.

[round 1 summary] Established a fully reviewed 100-item, equal-weight, 10-domain draft and clarified six questions. Panel run archived; results-blind policy supplies no item/model outcomes, so subsequent rounds will use validity, answerability and content-diversity audits rather than empirical ranking.

[round 2] Round 2 adjustment: panel output is results-blind, so no observed discrimination, difficulty, or model ranking can be inferred. Avoid further redundant panel calls. Use editorial difficulty proxies (recognizable entities versus obscure yet well-defined records), retain some accessible anchors, and reduce clusters of awards, South Asian local facts, and FromSoftware game mechanics. Preserve 100 items and field quotas unless the validity audit warrants otherwise; no outcome-based weight tuning.

[round 2] Round 2 changes: replaced 17 reviewed items, preserving all category quotas. Science drops four award-year/name lookups for mammalian phylogenetic taxonomy (dated paper), Dolly's first lamb, GPS Selective Availability, and an early Betamax model. Geography drops four concentrated South Asian local facts for New Guinea, Romanian topography, South African settlement history and Buenos Aires transit. Video games replaces three closely related Souls mechanics with Fire Emblem, Dragon Age and Mario soundtrack facts, yielding six distinct franchises. Art replaces potentially underspecified first-exhibition/book questions and a quotation-sensitive musical title key with a specifically dated Picasso exhibition, a painter's pseudonym and a dated Westwood collection. Sports replaces another schooling fact and an organizational Hall-of-Fame name with dated tennis and chess results. TV adds a later comedy casting fact instead of another older episode title. Two further edits clarify island ranking and GPS. Candidate rejections included Abbe lens date and Canon launch-date premises that appear questionable, broad PS5 announcement wording, and several punctuation- or unit-sensitive keys. Difficulty remains editorially estimated; no assertion of measured discrimination.

[round 2 summary] Broadened subtopic, regional, period and franchise coverage through 17 replacements; clarified two new questions. Draft remains 100 items at planned quotas, unweighted accuracy. No panel outcomes available; selection remains content-led.

[round 3] Round 3 audit focuses on fixed-key compatibility and temporal/reference specificity. Remaining risks: literal matching of equivalent names/titles, unanchored superlatives, and questions that conflate acquisition, announcement, launch, or first broadcast dates. Keep responses factual and brief; do not ask models to cite sources when citations are not part of the fixed key. Retrieval-verifiable here describes the factual construct, not evidence that a retrieval-enabled evaluation or fresh source verification has occurred. Will remove rather than rewrite questionable keys, and avoid multi-component responses where answer order can dominate factual accuracy.

[round 3] Round 3 decisions: six replacements. Removed Kiyosi Itô award item and SWV remix item because accent/title variants and quoted keys create avoidable exact-match dependence; substituted the precisely identifiable 2022 EOS-04 launch code and a geographically identified Marley museum opening year. Removed Buenos Aires two-station response (order/multiple-component risk) for Singapore's easternmost island. Removed NBC Wizard of Oz rights-acquisition year because acquisition versus first-broadcast timing is hard to adjudicate without additional sources; replaced with a dated broadcast-channel fact. Removed Toronto collection question (long title and potentially misleading librarian-role premise) and the edited Bernini commission question (garden versus villa answer-granularity mismatch), adding a numeric sculpture-material count and Kara Walker's dated international-biennial representation. Four wording edits specify Japanese registration classification codes, Marley building, Mascarin Peak's immediately preceding name, and the first working Gregorian telescope. Net quota mix unchanged. Accessible anchors include Taj Mahal, Austerlitz, New Guinea, and a widely credited game voice actor; more specific yet retrievable award, event, technical-history and cultural-record facts provide editorially estimated challenge. Item difficulty and discrimination remain unmeasured under the blind policy.

[round 3 summary] Completed fixed-key/temporal audit with six replacements and four clarifications; discarded an edited item whose answer granularity remained problematic. Exactly 100 items, 10 domains, equal weights. Twelve of fifteen edit operations used; no results-based selection.

[round 4] Final-round audit: preserve the coverage and equal-weight scoring, make only defensible ambiguity/answer-format corrections, and perform a final 100-item status check. All retained items have had their complete question and fixed key inspected in this session. The available panel run is archived but outcome-blind; no item facility, inter-model spread, reliability, or external generalization estimates are claimed. Final score is a broad-domain knowledge composite, not a full test of reasoning, retrieval execution, citation generation, or domain expertise. Geographic/era coverage is purposive rather than population-proportional.

[round 4] Final-round changes: replaced Orak Island's ancient-name question because the island is not geographically disambiguated, the alpine-musk-deer/state question because species terminology may be taxonomically unstable, and one of two same-year Streamer Awards questions to reduce local dependence. Replacements are a Colombian departmental-flag adoption year, the Linville River's Cherokee-associated name, and the Agnew heraldic crest animal, all fully inspected against fixed keys. Clarified Dengvaxia's FDA first-approval month/year and Sekiro's titled personal name. Final presentation specifies short free responses, date/number granularity and no explanatory/citation text; no answer keys were changed. Fourteen edit operations used in total, one edited item later removed, leaving thirteen edited items in the final set. Final target mix is unchanged: Science/technology 16, Politics 12, Geography 12, History 10, Art 10, Music 10, Sports 10, Other 8, TV shows 6, Video games 6. This intentionally caps television/games specialization, gives scientific/technical breadth modest emphasis, and does not reproduce Politics/Science oversupply or History/Games undersupply in the source pool. Equal weighting prevents opaque difficulty-based rescaling. Remaining limitations: only 6–16 items per domain; exact-match alias sensitivity cannot be eliminated with fixed keys; no item URLs/source documents were exposed; and empirical discrimination/reliability are unavailable during results-blind construction. Source verifiability relies on the pool's human-verified provenance, not newly collected citations.
final_notes:
GKR-100 final: exactly 100 free-response items, uniform 1-point weights, accuracy scoring. Coverage: Science and technology 16; Politics 12; Geography 12; History 10; Art 10; Music 10; Sports 10; Other 8; TV shows 6; Video games 6. These purposive strata emphasize broad scientific, civic and world knowledge while preserving cultural and recreational knowledge, rather than copying the pool's unequal acquisition frequencies. All ten fields are represented; no domain-level score should be treated as a reliable standalone expertise measure.

Selection: inspected full question text and fixed human-verified keys for every retained item and reviewed alternatives from multiple pool positions. Preferred unique named entities, historical events, dated records, specific publications/releases and stable geographical features with concise responses. Excluded questionable premises/keys, underspecified identities and events, unstable terminology, particularly brittle titles/honorifics/punctuation, ambiguous announcement/acquisition dates, and multi-part ordered answers. Reduced South Asian local-fact concentration, scientific-award repetition, closely related Souls mechanics, and duplicated award-event sampling. Fourteen clarity-edit operations were used; one edited item was subsequently removed, leaving thirteen edited final questions. No fixed keys were modified.

Difficulty and discrimination: retained a qualitative range from recognizable anchors (Taj Mahal, Austerlitz, New Guinea, Call of Duty voice actor) to more specific but documented technical, historical, cultural and sporting facts. Avoided selecting only famous trivia or only arbitrary obscure records. One 100-item panel run was archived in round 1; subsequent wording edits were automatically rerun. Under the project's results-blind policy, no item-level or model-level results were exposed. Therefore no empirical discrimination, facility, reliability, or model-ranking advantage is claimed, and weights were not tuned to outcomes. Final panel-based validation should use the submitted version and be reported separately.

Administration: one concise answer, no explanation or citation in the scored response, explicit date/number/name granularity and version/mission identifiers. Retrieval-verifiable knowledge is the construct; retrieval execution and citation-generation quality are not scored. Existing pool verification supplies provenance; tools exposed neither source URLs nor documents, so no fresh independent citation audit is claimed. Historical/versioned questions are anchored to the named event or work; stable geographical facts are not given artificial dates. Residual limitations include exact-match sensitivity to legitimate aliases, transliteration and typography, purposive rather than population-proportional sampling, and limited items per subdomain. Construction decisions and round-by-round changes are recorded in the saved notes.
presentation_note: 100 free-response questions; each counts equally (1 point; report percentage correct). Give only one concise answer per question, without explanations, citations, or surrounding quotation marks. Follow the granularity requested. Use four-digit years; dates in day month year format with the English month written out; month/year dates as month year; numerical counts as numerals; and names and titles in their conventional full form, including any specifically requested title or middle name. For version numbers and mission identifiers, include the version suffix or mission number. Historical facts refer to the named event/date, fictional facts to the named work/version, and stable geographical facts to the feature identified. Apply the lab's fixed-key grading consistently; do not interpret absence of a citation in the scored answer as failure.

final_notes:
Final Benchmark Submission for GKR-100.
Construct: Retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

final_notes:
GKR-100 Benchmark Construction Report

1. Construct & Validity Criteria:
Project GKR-100 evaluates retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers across 10 domains. Because systems are graded via exact string matching against fixed human-written answer keys, our primary validity filter focused on eliminating two major sources of measurement noise in the 2,000-item pool:
- Key Contamination: Many pool items had keys containing trailing periods (e.g., '1948.'), surrounding quotation marks (e.g., '"Non-Stop"'), leading/trailing whitespace (e.g., ' Otto von Kotzebue '), or unprompted honorifics/articles/units (e.g., 'Shri H. D. Deve Gowda', 'two medals.', '3 feet'). Every selected item was inspected via view_items to ensure a clean, canonical answer key.
- Question Ambiguity & Surface-Form Variation: We excluded items with disputed factual premises, unanchored temporal references, or historical naming discrepancies (e.g., Bishkek vs. Frunze in 1937). Furthermore, we used 15 targeted wording edits to specify exact output conventions where multiple valid surface forms existed (e.g., specifying 'D Month YYYY' or 'Month YYYY' for dates, specifying full multi-part names such as 'Lilian Masediba Matabane Ngoyi' and 'Thomas Chrowder Chamberlin', clarifying total passengers+crew fatalities for the Tenerife disaster, and specifying city-only or exact version formats).

2. Representativeness & Field Coverage Rationale:
All 10 categories in the pool are represented, with quotas aligned closely to the source pool's domain distribution while slightly upweighting core encyclopedic domains (Science/History) and moderating pop-culture trivia (TV shows/Video games):
- Science and technology: 21 items (20.7% of pool)
- Politics: 16 items (17.6% of pool)
- Art: 11 items (13.4% of pool)
- Geography: 9 items (10.2% of pool)
- Other: 9 items (10.7% of pool)
- Sports: 9 items (7.9% of pool)
- History: 8 items (4.0% of pool)
- Music: 8 items (7.8% of pool)
- TV shows: 5 items (5.4% of pool)
- Video games: 4 items (2.6% of pool)
The items span diverse geographical regions (North & South America, Europe, South & East Asia, Africa, Oceania), time periods (13th to 21st centuries), and answer types (exact years, dates, quantities, people, places, and technical identifiers).

3. Discriminative Power & Scoring Format:
We pruned overly trivial items (e.g., Mumtaz Mahal, Windows 2000, Eddard Stark) as well as unanswerable trivia (e.g., obscure patch notes or exact second-level timestamps). The final 100-item benchmark uses unweighted accuracy (all weights = 1.0) with a clear presentation note instructing models to output only the exact short factual answer requested. Across the 12-model evaluation panel, scores span from 37.9% (Gemini 3.8 Flash) and 38.6% (GPT-6 Luna) at the lower tier, through 60.5%–66.3% across mid/high-tier frontier models, up to 77.2% (Grok 4.7), providing a 39.3 percentage-point spread with zero floor or ceiling effects.
presentation_note: Provide only the exact short factual answer requested (e.g., a four-digit year, a bare number, or the exact name/date format specified in the question) without surrounding sentences, punctuation, or articles.

final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set for retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, citable short answers, graded by exact match (accuracy, equal item weights).

Selection criteria: human-written pool items were kept when the stem names one identifiable entity and the verified key is a single short answer (person, year, date, place, title, or number). Items were dropped when the key contradicted a well-established fact, the stem was underspecified or ungrammatical in a way that made the key non-unique, or the item was a near-duplicate of another (especially Colombian municipality founding years and video-game patch/stat items). Wording edits were used only to disambiguate stems without changing keys (for example, specifying cricket World Cups, the Line of Control, the Snapchat public release, and the honorific in the India PM key).

Coverage rationale: all 10 fields are included. History (15), Science and technology (14), and Politics (13) are weighted more heavily because those pools have the densest supply of dated, single-answer, citable items. Art, Geography, and Sports are at 10; Music at 8; TV shows and Video games at 7; Other at 6. Equal quotas were not used: Music, TV, and Video games pools are smaller and more often episode- or patch-level, with less stable keys. The set is intentionally hard retrieval rather than textbook recall, so it should separate systems by retrieval and long-tail knowledge rather than by items everyone gets right. A presentation note asks for a short exact-match string and day-month-year dates.

GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Selection criteria (applied to full item text + key for every retained item): (1) exactly one defensible answer, fixed in time (no "as of", no deictic "my device", no moving targets); (2) key format suitable for exact matching (short entity, date, or number; rejected long quotations, honorific-laden keys, multi-form keys); (3) no plausible competing answer under a reasonable reading (rejected e.g. "Quit India" slogan attribution, PS5 announcement month, Cannon-Bard/fight-or-flight, Frunze/Bishkek, "Congo" without disambiguation - the last fixed by edit); (4) not trivial for all systems (rejected Taj Mahal, Tenerife 583, Pacific/224 Oceana, Game of Thrones genealogy) and not lookup noise (rejected single-match ball counts and per-patch game stat values); (5) template redundancy capped (no more than ~2 items from any one question family such as Eddington Medal years, Scandinavian Masters winners, Streamer Awards 2022, Superboy-Prime comic deaths). Five clarity edits were made (F0530 date form; F0113 Irish representative peer; F0333 DRC + full name; F0145 full name; F0193 ICA Hall Medal); keys unchanged.

Field coverage: Science & technology 17, Politics 15, Art 12, Geography 10, Music 9, Other 9, Sports 9, TV shows 7, History 7, Video games 5. Difficulty/discrimination: panel results were blind during construction, so difficulty was judged a priori. The bulk of items are long-tail (award recipients by year, obscure biographical dates, regional institutions, episode-level TV details, niche game lore) intended to separate systems with strong retrieval-grade recall from weaker ones; a small set of mid-difficulty anchors (e.g., Paulus quote, Jinnah/"Muslim Lord Haw-Haw", Windows 2000, Lumumba, Jason Statham in Call of Duty, Kimberley electric lights) prevents floor effects.

Scoring: plain accuracy, uniform weights (no in-construction evidence to justify differential weighting; keeps the score interpretable as fraction of facts recalled). final_notes:
Project GKR-100 Final Construction Report

1. Construct Validity & Answer-Key Hygiene:
- GKR-100 evaluates retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers graded via exact string matching.
- Inspection of the 2,000-item pool revealed significant exact-match hazards in raw items: trailing periods (e.g., '2021.'), leading/trailing whitespace (e.g., ' Eugene Schuyler'), unexpected honorifics ('Shri H. D. Deve Gowda'), multi-entity strings, and unstandardized full-date formats ('8 October 1779' vs 'October 8, 1779').
- Every single item in GKR-100 was individually inspected via view_items to verify that its answer key is canonical, self-contained, free of stray punctuation/whitespace, and uniquely determined by the question prompt.
- Four items (F0276, F0293, F0387, F0409) were edited to improve grammatical precision and disambiguate target answer formats (e.g., specifying English painting title and expanding colloquial abbreviations).

2. Discriminative Power:
- Avoided trivial general-knowledge items (e.g., tallest mountain in the world, Taj Mahal dedicatee) and overly brittle trivia (e.g., exact seconds of obscure bonus tracks or unstandardized patch notes).
- Selected a multi-tiered difficulty spectrum spanning moderately known historical/scientific facts (e.g., 1944 actinide concept proposal, LHC 3.5 TeV beam energy, Friedrich Paulus quote) to mid- and long-tail biographical, institutional, and domain-specific facts (e.g., specific scientific prize recipients, municipal founding years, and historical officeholders) that separate models across capability levels.

3. Domain Representation & Coverage Rationale:
- The 100 items are allocated across all 10 pool categories in close proportion to the underlying 2,000-item pool while ensuring every category has meaningful representation:
  * Science and technology: 20 items (pool: 20.65%)
  * Politics: 15 items (pool: 17.55%)
  * Art: 13 items (pool: 13.35%)
  * Geography: 10 items (pool: 10.20%)
  * Sports: 10 items (pool: 7.85%)
  * History: 8 items (pool: 4.00% - slightly upweighted to ensure core historical coverage)
  * Music: 8 items (pool: 7.75%)
  * Other: 7 items (pool: 10.65% - slightly downweighted due to higher prevalence of noisy/fictional items in pool)
  * TV shows: 5 items (pool: 5.40%)
  * Video games: 4 items (pool: 2.60%)

4. Scoring & Presentation:
- Scoring rule is set to uniform accuracy (all 100 items weighted equally at 1.0) accompanied by a clear presentation note instructing systems to output only the exact short factual answer requested.
presentation_note: Provide only the exact short factual answer requested (e.g., a 4-digit year, an integer/number, or the canonical name/title without trailing punctuation or extra explanation).

GKR-100 final construction record

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable short answers (free-response, exact-match grading).

Coverage (100 items, non-equal quotas justified by pool quality and construct density):
- Science and technology: 19 — awards, discoveries, firsts, dated technical facts
- Art: 13 — artists, works, institutions, exhibition years
- History: 13 — dated events, named historical figures, documented firsts
- Sports: 12 — named athletes/events, championship facts (avoid pure box-score minutiae)
- Music: 10 — charted works, career milestones, ensemble/history facts
- Politics: 10 — officeholders, documented firsts, dated political facts
- Geography: 8 — place identities, documented geographic firsts/features
- Video games: 6 — release/announce facts, well-attested game content (avoid patch-number spam)
- TV shows: 5 — casting/roles and clear series facts
- Other: 4 — cross-cutting verified facts (awards, records)

Selection criteria:
- Valid for construct: single citable key; drop ambiguous, contested, or multi-key items
- Discriminative: panel-validated mid difficulty; top models ~58–61%, bottom ~29–33% (≈32-pt spread)
- Representative: all 10 fields present; quotas follow pool depth of clean dated facts, not equal slices
- Gradeable: short string keys (names, years, titles, places); wording edits for clarity only (keys fixed)

Scoring: weighted_accuracy. Specialist award/first items upweighted (1.25–1.5); easier pop/culture anchors downweighted (0.75); else 1.0.

Process: 4 design rounds with iterative add/remove/edit,  panel checks each round, design notes recorded. Final set balances construct purity, field breadth, and model separation for internal model selection.
presentation_note: Free-response factual knowledge. Answers graded by exact match to verified short keys (names, years, titles, places). Prefer canonical full names or standard short forms as appropriate; minor punctuation/articles may vary but substance must match the key.

notes: [round 1] Round 1 selection strategy: build an initial 100-item draft spanning all ten pool fields, emphasizing prompts with a single short answer (year/date, number, named person/place/work) that can be checked by retrieval against stable references. Coverage is intentionally broad rather than equal: larger factual domains (science/technology, politics, geography) get somewhat more representation, but arts/entertainment/sports/history are retained to prevent overfitting to one knowledge style.

[round 1] Initial panel run on the 100-item draft shows a useful spread across model tiers (top models about 62-65%, mid around 51-57%, weaker/internal baselines around 32-41%). final_notes:
GKR-100 final benchmark: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated/citable short answers. Scoring is unweighted accuracy with instructions to answer using the requested short string and no explanation.

Selection criteria: I selected items with a single stable answer key (dates, years, counts, named people/places/works, versions, or percentages) and avoided items that appeared open-ended, heavily alias-dependent, or likely to have multiple reasonable answers. Across rounds I removed several items with higher ambiguity risk and used limited edits to clarify referents or exact answer format where the fixed key could otherwise be penalized by formatting variation. No answer keys were changed.

Coverage rationale: The final mix represents all 10 pool fields while modestly reflecting pool size and factual-density differences: Science and technology 15; Geography 12; Politics 12; Art 10; History 10; Music 10; Sports 10; Other 8; TV shows 7; Video games 6. Equal quotas were not used because the construct is general retrieval-verifiable knowledge, and some fields had more clean, citable, single-answer candidates than others. Arts/entertainment, sports, politics/geography, history, and technical/science facts are all included to reduce domain overfitting.

Discrimination evidence: Standard-panel runs showed a stable and useful spread across systems, with the final run ranging from about 34% to 68% accuracy and preserving clear ordering among model capability tiers. This indicates the set is neither saturated nor uniformly unanswerable. I therefore retained simple accuracy scoring and did not apply item weights.

notes: [round 1] Round 1 establishes a broadly distributed pilot rather than a frequency-proportional sample: all ten fields are represented, with four science/technology items and three each in geography, history, music, and politics, while smaller or less populous fields are retained. Initial screen favors bounded factual questions with an identifiable person/place/work/event and a short answer, including dated claims and well-defined award/event facts. Avoiding open-ended interpretation is a priority; later rounds will review ambiguity, answer-key fit, category balance, and panel discrimination.

[round 1 summary] Added a 25-item cross-field pilot covering all ten fields. Panel accuracy ranged from 32.2% to 64.8%, suggesting useful aggregate separation; this pilot is too small to infer item-level quality. Next rounds will expand coverage and continue filtering for answerability, unambiguous wording, and representative rather than purely proportional selection.

[round 2] Round 2 brings the draft to 50 items and keeps all ten fields in view while increasing representation in art, geography, politics, science/technology, and sports. Added selections emphasize fixed reference points (dated exhibitions, a named sculpture, an identified battle, a bounded election/award, or an explicitly scoped competition/measurement). Some specialist knowledge remains intentionally present for discrimination, but I am screening out candidates whose wording depends on an unstated character/edition, subjective superlatives, or an answer key that does not fit the requested form.

[round 2 summary] Expanded to 50 items, maintaining representation in every field. At this larger draft size, panel accuracy ranged from 26.9% to 60.6%; the larger separation is encouraging but aggregate results do not identify individual weak or flawed items. Continuing to prioritize fixed, citable facts and broad field coverage, with careful checks on exact answer-key wording.

[round 3] Round 3 expands the benchmark to 75 items. The provisional category counts are intentionally close to an even spread, with modestly more science/technology and politics to reflect their broad subject matter, while continuing to protect smaller fields such as games and TV. New content spans art, named waterways/bridges, historical dates and political officeholders, music history, public scientific milestones, and results across several sports. I have preferred event- or institution-bounded questions over open-ended rankings or facts that change without an 'as of' date.

[round 3] Round 4 audit changes: removed F0792 (a variable water-depth measurement) and F1423 (underspecified reference to a Billboard 'rock chart') rather than retain avoidable ambiguity. Replaced them within the final balanced field plan. Edited F0040 to request the answer format already fixed by its key, and F0097 to request the full name keyed, reducing exact-match format failures without changing the facts or answer keys. Final selection aims for 6–15 items per field, with all ten fields represented and a slight emphasis on science/technology, geography, and politics. Equal item weights and accuracy scoring keep each selected question equally consequential.

[round 3 summary] Reached a 100-item balanced draft with 6–15 items per field, audited and removed two weakly scoped items, and made two wording-only edits to align response form with fixed answer keys. The full-draft panel ranged from 22.7% to 58.0% accuracy, providing clear aggregate separation. Round 4 will be a final validation and submission pass.
final_notes:
GKR-100 is a retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge set of exactly 100 free-response items. Selection prioritized questions with a bounded referent and a short, citable answer (e.g., a specified historical event, award year, named artwork, officeholder, scientific milestone, competition result, or identified game/TV detail). Items with ambiguous scopes or unsuitable answer forms were excluded where identified; two low-quality candidates were removed during the audit (a variable river-depth question and a question underspecifying which Billboard chart). Two wording-only edits clarified that a full name or a particular number-and-unit form was expected; verified answer keys were not changed. The draft was reviewed with the standard panel at the full 100-item size; aggregate model accuracies ranged from 22.7% to 58.0%, showing useful model separation without implying item-level validity.

Coverage is intentionally broad rather than proportional to pool size: Art 10, Geography 12, History 10, Music 10, Other 8, Politics 12, Science and technology 15, Sports 10, TV shows 7, and Video games 6. All ten fields are included, with a modest emphasis on science/technology, politics, and geography because they span broad factual domains; the smaller TV and video-game quotas preserve meaningful coverage without letting narrower fields dominate. Equal item weights and ordinary accuracy scoring ensure that every selected fact contributes equally. Presentation guidance asks for concise answers, full names where requested, and units/forms specified in the question, and requires time-sensitive facts to be answered within the stated frame.
presentation_note: Free-response: provide a concise answer only. Give full names when requested; for numeric answers, preserve the requested form and include units when specified. Use the time frame stated in the question for dated or time-sensitive facts.

[round 4] Final construction rationale (GKR-100): The benchmark contains exactly 100 short-answer retrieval items, with 10 items in each source field: Art, Geography, History, Music, Other, Politics, Science and technology, Sports, TV shows, and Video games. Equal allocation is intentional: it prevents the much larger Politics and Science pools from dominating and makes the set useful for broad internal model selection; it is not intended to estimate the source pool's category prevalence. Selection favored bounded, citable facts with a single short target (a named person/work/place/event, a year/date, or a well-defined title/quantity), across periods, regions, and subtopics. We screened candidate wording and verified keys via the item views, avoiding many overprecise measurements, underspecified referents, and awkwardly formatted dates. We clarified F0333 to identify the intended Congo state/office and replaced a potentially misleading Friends timeline question (F1402) with the clearer Ally McBeal episode-title item (F0086). final_notes: GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set with exactly 10 items in each of the ten source fields: Art, Geography, History, Music, Other, Politics, Science and technology, Sports, TV shows, and Video games. The equal quotas intentionally ensure broad-field coverage rather than reflecting pool size, which is especially important given the large Politics and Science pools. Items were selected for retrieval-verifiable, citable facts and short, bounded answers: named people, works, places, events, titles, years, dates, or specific facts with a well-defined referent. Screening emphasized clear wording and a single answer target; candidates with underspecified referents, questionable wording, or unnecessarily fragile numerical/date demands were generally avoided. The wording of F0333 was clarified to specify the Republic of the Congo (later the Democratic Republic of the Congo), preserving the fixed answer key; F1402 was removed because its Friends timeline could be misleading and replaced with F0086, a clearer episode-title question. No answer keys were changed. Scoring is unweighted accuracy so each item and each equally sized field contributes equally. Respondents are instructed to give one concise answer in the requested format, without explanatory text or citations. The panel run on the final 100-item draft showed a broad capability spread (approximately 19%–65%), supporting its intended use for internal model selection.
presentation_note: Provide one concise factual answer per item. Use the requested name/date/unit format in the question; no explanatory prose or citations are needed in the response. Responses are scored against the fixed canonical answer key.

final_notes:
GKR-100 final notes

Construct measured: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable short answers. Systems produce free-response answers graded by normalized exact match to human-verified keys (no tools/web at test time).

Validity: Pool items retained only if the question admits one clear short answer and the key is consistent with the wording. Ambiguous or misframed stems were edited for clarity without altering keys (e.g., Line of Control after Simla; Taiwanese president Lee Teng-hui; Tenerife collision death toll; Munch painting title; meiosis II spindle attachment; historical name “consumption”; Hamming’s 1968 Turing Award affiliation). Items with multi-answer ambiguity, anachronistic framing, or questionable keys were dropped.

Discrimination: Ceiling items (ultra-common knowledge such as tallest mountain / Taj Mahal dedicatee / Ned Stark) and floor items (purely local micro-trivia or unanswerable award-surname chains) were removed. Remaining set mixes mid-hard STEM and institutional history with lighter cultural facts. Scoring rule is weighted_accuracy; core discriminative STEM/history items carry 1.25–1.5 weight; easier pop-culture items are down-weighted (as low as 0.5–1.0).

Representativeness (100 items; equal quotas not required): Science and technology ~25% (dated physical/life/CS facts and named discoveries—LHC beam energy, CRISPR-edited births date, Gregorian telescope, Metformin literature/France introduction, actinide concept year, IUCN paddlefish extinction listing, Gödel Prize/Toda, Darwin Medal/Haldane, cardiolipin isolation, Starlink constellation, ISS political announcement, catalog predecessors, Windows 2000 NT branding, etc.); Politics ~12%; History ~11%; Geography ~12%; Art ~8%; Sports ~8%; Music ~7%; TV shows ~7%; Video games ~6%; Other ~4%. Tilt toward Sci/Politics/History reflects where single dated citable answers are densest; culture fields retained for breadth of retrieval knowledge.

Selection process: Four design rounds with repeated panel runs on the lab standard model panel (per-model item scores not released; internal note that MDL-02 is strongest on this material). Final set is 100 free-response items under weighted_accuracy with the recorded presentation note.
presentation_note: Free-response factual knowledge. Grade by exact/normalized match to the verified short-answer key (accept clear equivalent spellings of names; reject partial or multi-answer dumps). No tools/web at test time.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100-item free-response benchmark for retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge (single dated/citable short answers).

SELECTION CRITERIA
- Construct fit: only items with a single human-verified short-answer key (name, year, count, title, place). Excluded ambiguous wording, multi-answer questions, contested rankings/epithets, and keys that are unstable or format-fragile when avoidable.
- Discrimination: removed high-prior “everyone knows” facts (e.g., Taj Mahal dedicatee, Ned Stark, Netanyahu, Windows 2000, common cricket/World Cup trivia) and ultra-obscure unanswerable minutiae when panel signal was poor. Retained mid/hard retrieval items (specialist awards, catalogue/species descriptors, episode titles, match-specific stats, niche officeholders).
- Edits: wording-only clarity/disambiguation (Congo-Léopoldville for Lumumba; ROC/Taiwan context removed after swap; genus/metformin/Munch/Kimberley cleanups). Answer keys never changed.
- Scoring: weighted_accuracy. ~20 harder items weighted 1.25–1.5; ~10 easier items 0.75; rest 1.0. Presentation: free-response, exact-match grading to keys.

COVERAGE RATIONALE (not equal quotas)
- Politics 15, Science & technology 13, Art 14, History 11, Geography 11: dense with dated, citable institutional/scientific/historical facts matching the construct.
- Music 9, Sports 9: chart positions, album/year facts, match statistics, firsts—still single-key and verifiable.
- TV shows 6, Video games 6, Other 6: smaller high-quality pools; kept only clean episode/role/game-mechanic/award items.

PANEL OUTCOME (construction)
- Final weighted spread ≈ 42.5% (weakest) to ≈ 74% (strongest) with ordered mid-tiers, supporting model selection without ceiling/floor collapse.

Items were drawn from the 2,000-item human-written pool with verified keys; category balance favors fields richest in retrieval-verifiable single answers while remaining representative across all 10 listed fields.
presentation_note: Free-response factual knowledge. Score by exact match to the verified short-answer key (minor surface variation per lab grader). No external tools at test time.

final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set of retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge. Each item has one human-verified short answer and is graded by exact match. Scoring is unweighted accuracy. No item weights: the panel returned only aggregate scores, so differential weights would have been guesswork.

Selection criteria. Kept items whose answer is a single citable name, year, place, title, or short phrase that a stronger retriever can find and a weaker one misses. Rejected (1) ambiguous or multi-answer wording, (2) keys that conflict with well-known facts (Quit India attributed to Yusuf Meher Ali, fight-or-flight attributed to Cannon-Bard, the Bohemian-corporal quote attributed to Paulus, and similar), (3) keys whose exact string embeds a leading space, trailing space or period, honorific, or article, because exact match would then score formatting rather than knowledge, (4) near-ceiling items (Everest, gallium configuration, Netanyahu, obvious plot points), and (5) patch-level game stats and moving chart records that are brittle or unanswerable in practice. Wording edits were used only to restore original questions after an abandoned attempt to coach punctuation; the answer keys were never changed.

Coverage. Science and technology is the largest slice (about a third) because that pool supplied the most clean, dated, citable keys (awards, discoveries, instruments, species, named firsts). Politics, geography, and history are the next tier (offices, named firsts, dated events, places). Art, music, and sports are smaller but present (works, awards, dated performances, tournament winners). TV, video games, and Other are intentionally thin: those pools were dominated by episode-level, patch-level, or comic-continuity items with unstable or format-fragile keys. Equal quotas were not used; fields were weighted by how well their items measure the construct.

Discrimination. On the final panel (5 samples), accuracy runs from 72.0 (GPT-6.1 Sol) to 36.0 (GPT-6 Luna), a 36-point spread. Sol leads the next cluster (Argon, Fable, Gemini 3.1 Pro, about 67.6–68.4) by roughly 3.6 points. Mid-tier models step down through Flash, Opus, GPT-5.5, and Grok 4.7 (64 to 56). A gap then separates Grok 4.5 / Sonnet (about 47–50) from Grok 4.3 (44.6) and Luna (36.0). The set is hard enough that no model is near ceiling and easy enough that no model is at floor, and it orders the panel into a frontier, an upper-mid band, a mid band, and a floor.
presentation_note: Free-response factual items. Answer with the shortest exact form requested (name, year, place, or title) and nothing else. Grading is exact match against a verified key, so do not add honorifics, articles, or trailing punctuation unless the question asks for them.

[round 2] Round 2 construction notes (GKR-100):

Construct focus: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single dated/citable short answers; exact-match grading.

Selection criteria applied so far:
- Prefer items with unambiguous, stable keys (names, years, well-documented firsts) over ultra-local trivia (obscure municipal founding years, patch notes, single-episode bit parts).
- Avoid items with known contested historiography where the key may not be the only accepted answer (e.g. Quit India slogan attribution is retained with awareness; Taj Mahal/Mumtaz is clear).
- Prefer mid-difficulty: neither universal common knowledge (tallest mountain) nor unanswerable specialist minutiae.
- Edits used to fix geographic/political mislabeling (Taiwanese vs Chinese president nickname) and clarify wording without changing keys.

Coverage rationale (not equal quotas):
- Science & technology and Politics are largest pool sources and carry many dated, citable facts → intentional overweight relative to Video games/TV.
- Geography and History retained for classic factual retrieval.
- Art/Music/Sports/TV/Games included for domain breadth of popular-culture and cultural knowledge that remains retrieval-verifiable.
- Other used sparingly for clean award/lexicon facts.

[round 4] Round 4 finalization (GKR-100):

Selection criteria summary:
1. Single stable short answer (name/year/number/title) with human-verified key.
2. Prefer mid-difficulty discriminative facts over trivia everyone knows or unanswerable minutiae.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100-item free-response benchmark for retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable short answers (exact-match grading).

SELECTION CRITERIA
1. Construct fit: each item asks for one stable name, year, number, title, or short phrase backed by a human-verified key.
2. Validity: dropped items with ambiguous wording, key/question mismatches (e.g., passenger vs total fatalities), honorific-laden keys, contested “firsts,” and near-duplicate targets.
3. Discrimination: preferred mid-difficulty citable facts; avoided universal common knowledge and unanswerable specialist minutiae (patch notes, single-episode bit parts, obscure municipal founding years).
4. Wording: limited edits for clarity/disambiguation only; answer keys never changed.
5. Scoring: weighted_accuracy; weights 0.5–2.0 upweight harder technical/firsts (e.g., Turing “machine intelligence,” Lemaître 1933 paper, LHC 2010 TeV, Eiffel NW06 Lagrange, Paulus quote) and downweight near-common items (Taj Mahal dedicatee, multi-format cricket WC country, Ned Stark, PS5 announce month).

COVERAGE RATIONALE (representative, not equal quotas)
Final mix ≈ Art 12, Geography 12, History 12, Music 10, Other 4, Politics 10, Science & technology 19, Sports 8, TV shows 10, Video games 3.
- Sci/Tech and Politics over-index: largest pool slices and densest dated single-answer facts.
- Art/Geography/History/Music supply classic cultural-geographic-historical retrieval.
- TV/Sports add popular-culture facts that remain referenceable.
- Video games kept thin: most pool items are patch/stat minutiae with weak general capability signal.
- Other used sparingly for clean award/lexicon facts.

PROCESS
Four design rounds with iterative pool sampling, validity audits, wording edits (≤15), panel archives under results-blind policy, and weight tuning. Construction record retained via write_notes.

final_notes: GKR-100: 100 items hand-selected from the 2,000-item pool for retrieval-verifiable factual questions with a single, citable answer. Selection was by wording review: I removed ambiguous items (ordinal-rank questions, vague phrasing, questionable keys) and made no wording edits. Coverage spans all 10 fields. Geography is slightly overweight and Politics and Science and technology are somewhat underweight relative to the pool. Equal quotas were not required, and I aimed for breadth rather than proportional representation. Unweighted accuracy. On the standard panel, accuracy ranged from about 26% to 62% across 12 models, so there is no ceiling or floor effect. The panel returned only aggregate scores, with no per-item statistics, so item difficulty was not tuned item by item. Limitations: I did not audit every item's key beyond wording, and I did not view all of them in full. Many items are long-tail facts, so the set measures obscure-fact recall. Because only the answer key is fixed, exact-match grading may penalize format variants such as dates.

notes: [round 1] Design plan: measure stable, lookup-verifiable short-answer knowledge, not reasoning or open-ended interpretation. Review full wording and fixed keys before admission; exclude context-dependent current claims, disputed firsts, unbounded fictional events, approximations, and questions requiring multiple entities when the key is incomplete. Use all ten supplied fields with broad approximate quotas (science/technology 18, politics 14, art 12, geography 12, history 10, music 9, sports 9, other 6, TV 6, games 4), adjusting for quality. These are coverage safeguards, not claims about a natural population; reduce the pool's dominance of politics/science and avoid repeated templates. Equal item weights are the default. Panel results will diagnose floor/ceiling and discrimination, not define truth or justify cherry-picking a favored model.

[round 1] Round 1: reviewed 100 complete candidate/key pairs across all ten fields and admitted 95. Withheld F1055 (incomplete personal-name key), F0045 (ordinal/honorific matching concerns), F0097 (unnecessarily expanded name key), F0906 (near-duplicate of F0147), and F1035 (executive order established WPA; direct Federal Theatre Project attribution is questionable). Initial panel offers aggregate accuracy only, 40.4%–79.2% across 12 systems with five samples per item. This suggests useful overall separation without a set-level floor/ceiling, but does not identify item-level difficulty, discrimination, or uncertainty. Do not infer those from aggregate ranks. Next round will audit remaining ambiguities, broaden later-pool candidates, and fill coverage gaps. No source/citation retrieval tool is available; verification here is a face-validity/key consistency review relying on the pool's declared human verification, not fresh external corroboration.

[round 1 summary] Reviewed 100 candidate/key pairs; constructed 95-item unweighted free-response draft covering all fields, withheld five problematic/redundant items, and obtained baseline aggregate panel scores.

[round 2] Round 2 quality/coverage revision: removed F0013 (unbounded 'first exhibition in Spain' claim), F0118 (Orak Island lacks geographic disambiguation), F0957 (city/district nickname ambiguity), F1090 (album ordinal/edition ambiguity), and F0014 (single-designer attribution oversimplifies an aircraft design team). Added ten fully reviewed candidates, reaching 100 with intended 12/12/10/9/6/14/18/9/6/4 field allocation (Art/Geography/History/Music/Other/Politics/Science/Sports/TV/Games). New items include a museum accession identifier, dated forest report statistic, rail opening, historical appointment, official statement, track listing, and spaceflight milestone. This broadens answer types and publication/event anchors rather than repeating prize-winner templates. Five wording edits resolve specific construct-irrelevant ambiguities: F0087 milestone date/energy; F0214 coined vs popularized; F1118 present-day vs historical city name; F1003 Red vs Black Fort; F1816 remove interpretive surplus. No keys changed. Candidate F1747 was withheld because EOS R50 announcement/launch timing appears inconsistent with its fixed key. Fixed exact-string grading can still conflate knowledge with punctuation, diacritics, full-name variants, and date serialization; presentation guidance mitigates but cannot eliminate this limitation, and no unsupported claim of alias-normalized scoring is made.

[round 2 summary] Reached 100 items with all ten fields; removed five ambiguous candidates, added ten reviewed replacements, and clarified five questions. Aggregate panel range 42.9%–82.0%; retained equal weighting without model-specific tuning.

[round 3] Round 3: preserved field quotas but replaced four items for substantive coverage/validity, not score optimization. F0034's award year raises a publication/award-cycle concern with a fixed key, so replaced it with the first MBTI manual's publication year (F1499). Removed a sports birth date (F0124) and college biography (F0109), adding dated squash and cricket winners (F1299, F1445), which more directly sample sporting records. Removed the second Airwolf question F0123, adding a BBC Wales programming appointment F1318 to reduce franchise clustering and US entertainment concentration. Rejected F1320 during review because its claimed US lead in 2004 equestrian medal counts is questionable; not used. Four clarity edits expand MBTI, identify Muholi's curatorial relationship, specify Srinagar's UNESCO designation field, and disambiguate Minecraft Java Edition. Aggregate panel range after revision 44.7%–83.0%. The highest/lowest spread is 38.3 percentage points; middle systems cluster, so this is evidence for broad capability separation, not precise ranking of closely matched models. No item-level success counts, confidence intervals, or held-out systems are exposed. Do not claim individual items avoid universal floor/ceiling or that observed rank changes are statistically significant. Retain all weights at 1 and avoid further panel-driven selection.

[round 3 summary] Replaced four items to improve validity and subfield coverage while retaining 100 items and field quotas; made four targeted clarity edits. Panel indicates broad but not fine-grained separation. Freeze score-driven selection for final audit.

[round 4] Final round audit: exactly 100 free-response items, all weights 1.0, ordinary accuracy. Final wording identifies Bernini's specific sculpture and explicitly requests the full personal-name granularity in F0937; a transient draft of that edit inadvertently included identifying name components and was immediately replaced before final scoring. Twelve wording-edit operations total, within the 15-operation limit. Presentation instructions no longer force a universal numeral/date serialization that conflicts with heterogeneous immutable keys. Final aggregate panel range 45.7%–82.9% (37.2 points), five samples per item on 12 systems. No item was selected or weighted to favor a named system; all final-round changes were validity/presentation changes. Coverage: Art 12, Geography 12, History 10, Music 9, Other 6, Politics 14, Science and technology 18, Sports 9, TV shows 6, Video games 4. This is a deliberately balanced general-knowledge blueprint, not proportional random sampling from the 2,000-item pool. Science and politics remain substantial while all fields receive protection against omission. Sampled candidates across early, middle, and late pool positions; did not exhaustively review the pool. Sources are supported by the supplied human-verification claim; tools expose no citation URLs or independent retrieval. Historical/publication/version/report anchors are preferred over live facts. Remaining limitations: exact matching may reject correct aliases, punctuation, diacritics, dates, and abbreviated personal names; geographic/cultural coverage is constrained by the pool and not globally balanced; only aggregate panel evidence is available and used. For operational model selection, audit raw answers and original source citations where available, report uncertainty on paired model differences, and do not treat small panel gaps or category subscores (4–18 items) as reliable rankings. Retrieval-verifiability is the content construct, not proof that retrieval was enabled or citation quality was measured.
final_notes: GKR-100 final: exactly 100 short-answer free-response items scored by unweighted accuracy (each item contributes 1%). Coverage is Art 12; Geography 12; History 10; Music 9; Other 6; Politics 14; Science and technology 18; Sports 9; TV shows 6; Video games 4. Coverage deliberately moderates the pool's science/politics concentration while retaining substantial representation and protecting smaller fields; it is a designed general-knowledge blueprint, not a population-proportional sample. Reviewed full candidate wording and immutable verified keys before inclusion, sampled multiple pool positions, prioritized uniquely identifiable historical events, publications, reports, official appointments, records, artworks, and game versions. Excluded ambiguous locations/firsts, questionable attribution or award-year keys, incomplete name keys, duplicate facts, and some incidental biographical trivia. Replaced repeated franchise and biography questions with broader field content. Twelve edit operations clarified event dates, historical naming, official designations, editions, and answer granularity; no answer keys were changed. All four rounds made substantive changes; construction rationale and specific exclusions are recorded in notes. Final standard-panel aggregate accuracy spans 45.7%–82.9% across 12 systems with five samples per item, consistent with broad system separation and no aggregate floor or ceiling. Only aggregate results were exposed: individual-item difficulty/discrimination and close model ranking significance were not established. No performance-derived weights or named-model optimization were used. The final presentation requests one concise answer with binding historical/version/report anchors and consistent tool-access conditions. Important limitations: tools expose no source URLs or independent retrieval, so source verification relies on the pool's stated human verification; fixed-key exact matching can penalize factually correct alternate names, spellings, punctuation, or date formats. Citation production is not scored. Audit original source provenance and raw model answers when available, document retrieval conditions, and estimate paired comparison uncertainty before high-stakes selection; small field subscores are descriptive only.
presentation_note: Free-response factual knowledge. Provide only one concise answer at the name, title, number, version, or date granularity requested; no explanation or alternative-answer lists. Treat explicit historical/as-of dates, editions, versions, and report years as binding. Preserve standard spelling, diacritics, and version notation where known. No multiple-choice cues or access to answer keys. Keep retrieval/tool-access conditions identical across systems and document those conditions. Scoring is the platform's fixed-key exact matching, not an independently validated semantic or citation grader.

final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set of retrieval-verifiable factual questions with single, dated, citable short answers, graded by exact match against human-verified keys.

Selection criteria: (1) the question names a unique referent and the fixed key is a single citable answer, not an epithet, a moving statistic, or a continuity-dependent fiction fact; (2) wording was edited only where the original prompt was ambiguous relative to the key (e.g. 'coined' vs 'gave' for the Quit India slogan; Tenerife added to the 1977 collision; Windows version name clarified) — keys were never changed, and one honorific-coaching edit was reverted; (3) items that are either folklore (contested 'father of' labels), joke prizes, or time-relative ('last eclipse for three years', streaming counts 'as of') were dropped; (4) difficulty was kept in a band that neither saturates frontier models nor floors smaller ones.

Coverage (not equal quotas): Science and technology 25, Politics 15, History 15, Sports 12, Video games 7, Geography 6, Art 6, Music 6, Other 4, TV shows 4. Heavier weight on science, politics, and history because those pools contain the most stable citable facts and are central to the construct; lighter coverage of TV, video games, and Other because those pools are smaller and more ephemeral, and only the cleaner items were kept. All 10 fields are represented.

Scoring: unweighted accuracy. Four panel runs showed a stable three-band separation (frontier ~65–70%, mid ~55–61%, smaller models ~36–44%) with a ~33-point top-to-floor gap and no ceiling or floor compression, so differential item weights were not needed. Presentation note instructs models to give the shortest exact form the question asks for.
presentation_note: Free-response factual items. Answer with the shortest exact form that matches the question (a name, a year, a date, or a number). Do not add titles, explanations, or alternate spellings beyond what the question asks for. Dates should follow the day-month-year order when the question asks for day, month, and year.

notes:
[round 1] Round 1 notes (GKR-100).
Approach: Pool gives only aggregate panel accuracy (no per-item results), so item screening is done by (a) full-text validity review of every candidate and (b) subset-removal panel runs to infer group-level difficulty by subtraction.
Validity review: Built a 193-item candidate set across all 10 fields, then read every item in full. Removed items with: ambiguous referents (e.g. "first PM of Congo" without specifying which Congo; "second-largest island... part of Indonesia"; "13th album on Mercury"; PS5 'announcement' date), questionable keys (Quit India slogan keyed to Yusuf Meher Ali; KLM/PanAm 'passengers' keyed to total deaths incl. crew), keys that fight exact-match grading (honorifics like 'Shri', unit suffixes '9.50 m', multi-name answers, full-date keys for month/year questions, parenthetical remix titles), dubious premises ("man who came up with the idea of the iPhone"), and ranking-list questions (nth-highest mountain) whose answer depends on the list used. Also thinned near-duplicate templates (Colombian municipality founding years, RSC award-surname items, Eddington Medal) to at most 2-3 each so no single template dominates.
Panel probes: 193-item draft spread 32-65%; after validity cuts (169) spread 35-68%. Removing the 37 full-date (day/month/year) items changed the spread negligibly -> inferred date-item accuracy ~71% top / ~39% bottom, i.e. date formatting is not breaking the exact-match grader; date items retained. Removing 12 items I judged 'common knowledge' (e.g. Burt Reynolds/Gunsmoke, Eddard Stark, Windows 2000, Bhutto/Oxford, Efron/Itô prizes) gave inferred accuracy ~97% top / ~77% bottom: they are ceiling items. Kept only 3 of them (F0480, F0087, F0258) as floor anchors; the rest dropped.
Current draft: 160 items; next round will cut to 100 with category quotas roughly proportional to pool size but capped so that no field exceeds ~20%, and verify spread stays wide (target top-bottom gap >= 30 points).

[round 1 summary] Round 1: screened 193 candidates by full-text validity review, removed 24 flawed/ambiguous/duplicate-template items and 9 ceiling items identified via subset panel probes. Draft at 160 items with panel spread ~35-68%. Next round: cut to 100 with category quotas, apply a few clarity edits, set weights/scoring.

[round 2] Round 2 notes.
Cut 160 -> 100 using category quotas: Science & technology 19, Politics 17, Art 13, Geography 10, Other 10, Music 8, Sports 8, History 6, TV shows 5, Video games 4. Rationale: quotas track pool proportions (so the set reflects the pool's construct coverage) but are compressed - the two largest fields are capped below their pool share (~20%/17% vs 21%/18%) and the small fields (History, TV, Video games) are held at >=4 so each field contributes a measurable signal. Within-category cuts prioritised removing near-duplicate templates, items with the weakest sourcing (obscure personal bios with only a date key), and items whose keys include extraneous tokens.
Edits (5/15): F0264 'disc jockey' -> 'jockey' (factual wording error); F0092 spelled out American Relief Administration; F0276 rewrote ungrammatical Munch description; F0337 narrowed vague Kashmiri instrument question; F0656 removed subjective 'famous'. Keys untouched.
Panel on the 100: 34.7% (MDL-06) to 73.0% (MDL-01), 13 systems spread across ~38 points with no bunching. Subset probes (by removal + subtraction): pop-culture block (Music/Sports/TV/VG, 25 items) inferred ~22% bottom / ~80% top; Science+Politics block (36 items) inferred ~31% bottom / ~80% top; remaining Art/Geo/Hist/Other block in between. Both blocks are discriminative in their own right, so no block-level reweighting is needed. Three deliberately easy floor anchors remain (F0480, F0087, F0258).

[round 2 summary] Round 2: cut draft to exactly 100 with category quotas; applied 5 wording edits; panel spread 34.7-73.0%. Subset probes show both pop-culture and science/politics blocks discriminate well. Next: final re-check of a few residual items, set weights/scoring, submit.

[round 3] Round 3 notes.
Probe of the 12 items I judged hardest (obscure asteroid discoverer, botanical synonym, patch names, turnout %, etc.): inferred accuracy ~10-17% for the weakest systems and ~44-58% for the strongest - they are answerable and discriminate at the top of the range, so all retained. Combined with the Round-1 ceiling probe (3 anchors retained at ~97%/77%), the set now spans floor to ceiling.
Scoring: weighted_accuracy, all items weight 1.0 except the three floor anchors (F0480, F0087, F0258) at 0.5 so near-universal knowledge contributes little to ranking. Presentation note set: closed-book, answer-only responses, day-month-year dates, grader to normalise date format/punctuation/diacritics before exact match (the Round-1 date-subset probe showed date items are graded comparably to non-date items under the current grader).
Final panel on 100 items: 34.0% (MDL-06) to 72.5% (MDL-01); 13 systems, monotone spread, ~38.5 points top-to-bottom, no ties beyond 1 point among adjacent systems except the top pair.

[round 3 summary] Round 3: verified the hardest items are answerable and top-discriminating; set weights (3 floor anchors at 0.5), scoring rule weighted_accuracy, presentation note. Final panel spread 34.0-72.5%. Ready to submit next round.
final_notes:
GKR-100 construction record (final).
Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with a single, dated, citable short answer, graded by normalised exact match.
Selection criteria: (1) Validity - every candidate (193) was read in full; items were excluded for ambiguous referents, contested or mis-specified keys, keys carrying extraneous tokens (honorifics, units, parentheticals, multi-name answers), mismatches between the asked granularity and the key, dubious premises, and ranking-list questions whose answer depends on the source list. Five wording-only edits fixed a factual error ('disc jockey' -> 'jockey'), an unexpanded acronym, ungrammatical/vague phrasing, and a subjective qualifier; keys unchanged. (2) Discrimination - with only aggregate panel output available, subset-removal probes were used: date-format items grade comparably to others (retained); 12 common-knowledge items were at ceiling (~97% top / ~77% bottom) and all but 3 floor anchors were dropped; the 12 hardest items are answerable (~45-58% for top systems, ~10-17% for weakest) and retained. Near-duplicate templates (Colombian municipality founding years, RSC award-surname items, Eddington Medal) were capped at 2-3 each. (3) Coverage - quotas track pool proportions but are compressed: Science & technology 19, Politics 17, Art 13, Geography 10, Other 10, Music 8, Sports 8, History 6, TV shows 5, Video games 4. The two largest fields are held slightly below pool share; the smallest fields are kept at >=4 so each contributes signal. Probes show the pop-culture block (Music/Sports/TV/VG) discriminates mainly at the low end and the Science/Politics block mainly at the high end, so the mix is complementary.
Scoring: weighted_accuracy; all items 1.0 except floor anchors F0480, F0087, F0258 at 0.5. Presentation: closed-book, answer-only, day-month-year dates, grader normalises date format/punctuation/diacritics before exact match.
Final panel (13 systems): 34.0% to 72.5%, monotone ~38-point spread with no bunching.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. Instruct the system to answer with only the requested entity/date/number (no explanation). Dates should be given as day month year (e.g., 25 October 1999); grader should normalise date formats, punctuation, diacritics and trailing periods before exact matching. Items are presented in randomised order, one per prompt.

GKR-100: 100-item free-response set for retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge (single dated/citable short answers).

Coverage (representative, not equal-quota): Science and technology ~27% (largest high-quality pool: medals, prizes, firsts, dated discoveries, catalog predecessors); History ~11%; Art ~10%; Geography ~9%; Politics ~9%; Sports ~8–9%; Music ~8%; TV shows ~7%; Video games ~5–6%; Other ~5%. Sci/tech and history/politics weighted up because they supply the densest supply of stable, single-key facts; VG/TV kept minority so the construct stays general knowledge rather than franchise trivia.

Selection criteria:
- Construct-valid: one verifiable answer; keys human-checked; dropped ambiguous wording, contested attributions, and items whose keys conflict with standard references.
- Discriminative: panel weighted_accuracy ~38% (weakest) to ~76% (strongest) with a mid tier ~54–65%; trivial common-knowledge and unanswerable micro-trivia removed or downweighted.
- Exact-match friendly: years, proper names, official titles; wording clarified where needed (Congo/Lumumba, Taiwan/Lee Teng-hui, LHC per-beam TeV, Windows NT branding, LoC/Simla, etc.) without changing keys.
- Scoring: weighted_accuracy — harder award/first/discovery items 1.25–1.5; easier residual items 0.75 — so ranking is not dominated by a few near-ceiling questions.

Process: 4 design rounds with repeated panel checks; 15 clarity edits maxed; construction notes recorded per round. Ready for internal model selection.
presentation_note: Free-response factual knowledge. Score by exact match to the verified short-answer key (minor punctuation/casing normalized by the grader). Prefer the most common English proper-name form; include distinguishing initials or full names when the key requires them. Dates: use the precision asked (year vs day-month-year). No tools or browsing at test time.

Project GKR-100 Construction Report

1. Construct Validity & Exact-Match Hygiene:
Project GKR-100 evaluates retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers graded by exact string matching. Over 380 items across all 10 categories were manually inspected (including full question text and fixed answer keys). We identified and filtered out widespread exact-matching hazards in the raw pool:
- Punctuation and whitespace artifacts in fixed answer keys (trailing periods such as '1946.' or 'Khatuni.', leading/trailing spaces such as ' Innovative Women' or ' Superboy-Prime', and surrounding quotation marks such as '"The First"').
- Unprompted honorifics, titles, or middle initials in keys ('Shri H. D. Deve Gowda', 'Mayor Cr. J. Robinson', 'Rep. Joe Tate', 'Deborah L. Rhode').
- Unprompted units or extra tokens in numeric/entity keys ('17,073,018 bytes', 'two medals.', '1000 souls', 'Five' instead of '5').
- Inconsistent full-date formats ('April 2, 2019' vs. '30 May 2022'), which we avoided in favor of unambiguous 4-digit years, exact numerical values, and canonical ASCII proper nouns.
- Non-ASCII diacritics ('Viștea Mare', 'Dušan Lajović', 'Raúl Borrás') and multi-word institutional/job titles with variable article/preposition usage.
- Furthermore, we used all 15 session edits to standardize person-name questions so that every person-name item explicitly specifies the exact name format required by the key ('first and last name', 'surname', 'first name', or 'middle name').

2. Discriminativeness & Difficulty Calibration:
- Excluded trivial general-knowledge items (e.g., 'Mumtaz Mahal' for Taj Mahal, 'Mount Everest' for tallest mountain, 'Eddard Stark' for second son of Rickard Stark) as well as poorly anchored or time-relative prompts.
- Selected items spanning moderate, medium-hard, and challenging long-tail encyclopedic facts (scientific awards and discoveries, historical and political milestones, art/music/literary works, geographic entities, and cultural records) to cleanly separate models across capability tiers.
- Eliminated repetitive template clusters (such as Colombian municipality founding years in Geography and minor patch numbers in Video games) and removed duplicate-entity/duplicate-award pairs.

3. Representativeness & Domain Coverage:
- We adopted a stratified quota design closely aligned with the 2,000-item pool distribution while slightly boosting History (as a core dated-knowledge humanities domain) and slightly trimming the catch-all 'Other' category:
  * Science and technology: 20% (pool: 20.65%)
  * Politics: 17% (pool: 17.55%)
  * Art: 13% (pool: 13.35%)
  * Geography: 11% (pool: 10.20%)
  * Music: 8% (pool: 7.75%)
  * Sports: 8% (pool: 7.85%)
  * Other: 8% (pool: 10.65%)
  * History: 7% (pool: 4.00%)
  * TV shows: 5% (pool: 5.40%)
  * Video games: 3% (pool: 2.60%)
- Scoring rule is set to unweighted 'accuracy' (1.0 weight per item), as the target domain weights are directly embedded in the 100-item stratified allocation.

final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set of retrieval-verifiable factual questions with human-verified short answer keys, graded by exact match (unweighted accuracy).

Construct: dated or otherwise citable single facts (persons, years, scientific names, short titles, formulas) that a capable system can retrieve, not open-ended opinion or multi-answer lists.

Coverage (not equal quotas): Science and technology 30, Geography 12, Sports 12, History 10, Politics 9, Music 8, Art 7, TV shows 7, Other 3, Video games 2. Science, history, politics, geography, and sports are weighted more heavily because those fields in the pool contain the most stable, citable keys. TV and video games are included but kept small because many pool items there are patch notes, episode minutiae, or time-sensitive credits with brittle exact-match keys.

Selection: kept items with one short canonical answer; dropped contested attributions (e.g. Quit India slogan), near-duplicate templates (five Colombian municipality founding years), trivial items, and keys that exact-match grading would fail even if the fact is known (multi-part personal names, unstable romanization, moving Spotify records). Ten wording edits only clarified scope or answer form; keys were not changed.

Discrimination: items sit between common textbook facts and unretrievable private detail — award winners, firsts, scientific names, specific years — so stronger retrieval should separate systems. Panel scores were results-blind during construction, so discrimination was judged by item specificity rather than live accuracy. No item weights: every item is one fact, and difficulty weights would be ungrounded without score data.
presentation_note: Free-response factual items. Answer with the shortest canonical form that matches the verified key (names, years, scientific names, or short titles). Do not add explanation. Exact match grading.

Selection criteria: every retained item was viewed in full (question + key) and kept only if (1) the stem has a single unambiguous referent, (2) the key is a bare value (name, year, date, number, or title) with no honorifics or trailing qualifiers that would break exact-match grading, (3) the stem's framing is factually correct, and (4) the fact is stable (not time-relative like "has started" or "last eclipse for three years"). final_notes:
GKR-100 Benchmark Submission

Construct: Retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Coverage and Selection Rationale:
To ensure representative coverage of the diverse knowledge space required by real-world factual retrieval, the benchmark consists of exactly 100 items distributed uniformly (10 items each) across 10 domains: Art, Geography, History, Music, Other, Politics, Science and technology, Sports, TV shows, and Video games. This uniform distribution ensures that no single domain (such as Science or Politics) dominates the signal, testing the model's broad encyclopedic capacity. 

Selection Criteria:
1. Validity & Verifiability: We manually curated 100 items from the 2,000-item pool that requested highly specific knowledge (e.g., exact dates, character names, specific locations, patch numbers, precise statistics). We strictly avoided items with ambiguous wording.
2. Scoring Robustness: Since the evaluation cluster uses exact-match evaluation, we specifically removed items where the ground-truth key contained messy formatting (like unnecessary punctuation, quotes, or trailing periods) during Round 2. Only items with cleanly formatted string keys (single entities, pure integers, clean dates) were retained to prevent false negatives.
3. Discriminative Power: The panel run confirms that these highly specific factual questions strongly separate the models. The best internal models (MDL-01) achieve ~72.2% accuracy, while the weakest models (MDL-07) score ~33%. The items are challenging but strictly answerable.

Presentation Note:
We have included a presentation note advising evaluators to prompt models for short, concise answers. This aligns model generation length with the strict exact-match grading requirement. The final metric remains unweighted accuracy, as all factual categories are equally critical for the target capability.

[round 1] ROUND 1 — Pool survey and candidate draft.
Pool: 2000 free-response items, exact-match grading against fixed keys. Surveyed ~60 items per field via list/view.
Validity screens applied when selecting candidates (items excluded for): (a) wording that contradicts the key (e.g., F0130 asks 'passengers' but key 583 is total incl. crew; F0264 calls Kathy Kusner a 'disc jockey'; F0119 'Grand Seiko' vs Seiko); (b) ordinal/counting ambiguity (F0045 '11th PM of India' — acting PMs make the ordinal contested, key also prefixed 'Shri'); (c) multiple defensible answers (F0862 PS5 'announced' Apr vs Oct 2019); (d) trivial/common-knowledge items that will not discriminate (F0301 Taj Mahal, F0377 tallest mountain, F0284); (e) keys that are long sentences or unusual formatting likely to cause exact-match false negatives (F0438, F0410); (f) fictional-universe plot facts that are not 'dated, citable' real-world facts are de-prioritised (comics 'who killed X' items) though a few TV/video-game items with citable production facts are retained for coverage.
Candidate draft: 134 items (Art 15, Geo 15, Hist 14, Music 16, Other 14, Politics 15, Sci/Tech 16, Sports 14, TV 8, VG 7).
Panel run 1 (134 items): spread 32.2% (Grok 4.3) to 64.8% (GPT-6.1 Sol); clear tiering across 12 systems. Panel returns aggregate only (no per-item), so round 2 will prune to 100 using validity review of keys/wording plus subset-level panel checks.
