final_notes:
GKR-100 — 100 free-response items, retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

SELECTION CRITERIA
1. Construct fit: each item asks for one real-world, citable fact (person, date, year, place, title, number) that can be verified against a source. Fictional-plot facts (TV character genealogy, in-game lore/stat trivia) were excluded; only production/release facts from TV and video games were retained.
2. Validity: items were dropped when (a) wording contradicted or mis-specified the key (e.g., 'passengers' vs total deaths; mislabelled occupations), (b) the premise or ordinal was contested (e.g., 'Nth Prime Minister/Governor' counts, 'who came up with the idea of the iPhone', 'announced' with two defensible dates), (c) the key had exact-match hazards (prefixes like 'Rev.', suffixes like '18 episodes', long titles, multi-part answers, varying decimal percentages, verbatim quotations).
3. Discrimination: trivial common-knowledge items (Taj Mahal, tallest mountain, Lumumba, Windows 2000, etc.) were excluded. Panel evidence (aggregate-only): 33.0% (GPT-6 Luna) to 66.1% (GPT-6.1 Sol), monotone by model generation, no ceiling or floor compression. Two subset diagnostics confirmed that the 15 full-date items (implied ~54–73%) and the 9 TV/VG items (implied ~14–66%) are answerable and discriminating rather than dead weight.
4. Edits (3/15): F0092 expanded acronym ARA; F0193 specified the ICA Hall Medal; F0213 normalized phrasing and added country. Keys untouched.

COVERAGE (final): Art 13, Geography 12, History 12, Science & technology 12, Sports 11, Other 11, Music 10, Politics 10, Video games 5, TV shows 4. Rationale: near-even coverage of the eight real-world knowledge fields so no field dominates the score (the pool's Politics/Sci-Tech skew was not reproduced); TV/Video games kept small (9%) because few pool items there fit the construct. Within fields, items span regions (South Asia, Latin America, Africa, Europe, North America, East Asia) and eras (13th c. to 2023).

SCORING: plain accuracy, uniform weights (no per-item panel data to justify differential weights). Presentation note: short answer only; dates as day month year; exact match with light normalization.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. Systems must give only the short answer (name / year / date / number / title) with no explanation. Dates should be given as day month year (e.g., 8 October 1779); years as four digits; names as commonly written. Graded by exact match against the fixed key with standard normalization (case, punctuation, leading/trailing whitespace, honorific-free).

[round 1] Round 1 Design Notes:
1. Pool Audit & Validity Findings:
   - Inspected ~250 items across all 10 categories using view_items.
   - Identified widespread exact-match validity hazards in the raw pool:
     (a) Trailing periods or leading/trailing whitespace in keys (e.g., F0036 'Khatuni.', F0037 '1949.', F0080 ' Vivekanandapuri', F1961 '36.').
     (b) Surrounding quotation marks in keys (e.g., F0024 '"Right Here (Human Nature Remix)"', F0056 '"The First"').
     (c) Non-canonical prefixes, titles, or units embedded in keys (e.g., F0026 'Mayor Cr. J. Robinson', F0040 'two medals.', F0045 'Shri H. D. Deve Gowda', F1017 '42 injuries. ', F1987 '2,700G').
     (d) Key/question mismatches and multi-entity answers violating the 'single, dated, citable answers' construct (e.g., F0043 asking for two people; F0094 asking for month and year while key is 'June 4, 2021'; F0028 asking for a year range '1984 to 1986').
     (e) Repetitive template clusters (e.g., dozens of Antioquia/Boyacá Colombia municipality founding years in Geography).
2. Field Coverage Strategy:
   - Adopted a stratified domain allocation across all 10 categories reflecting pool proportions while ensuring core encyclopedic domains are well represented: Science and technology (19), Politics (16), Art (13), Geography (11), History (8), Music (8), Sports (8), Other (8), TV shows (5), Video games (4).
3. Round 1 Panel Evaluation:
   - Uncurated baseline (F0001-F0120) yielded compressed scores (32.2% to 64.8%, 32.6 pp spread) due to noisy keys.
   - Curated 100-item draft improved top-to-bottom spread to 42.4 pp (39.8% to 82.2%).
   - Split-block diagnostics (Block A: 25 items, Block B: 25 items, Second 50 items) revealed that Block A achieves a 55.2 pp spread (25.8% to 81.0%), whereas the Second 50 has a narrower 31.6 pp spread (43.4% to 75.0%) with more trivial items solved by the weakest model (MDL-07). In Round 2, we will dissect the Second 50 and replace overly easy/non-discriminative items with stronger verified items.

[round 1 summary] Completed Round 1 pool audit, established stratified 10-category coverage (100 verified clean-key items), and ran split-block panel diagnostics showing a 42.4 pp capability spread across the 13-model panel.

[round 2] Round 2 Design Notes:
1. Diagnostic Dissection of Round 1 Second 50 (Blocks C & D):
   - Evaluated Block C (25 items: Geography, History, Music) and deduced Block D (25 items: Sports, Other, TV shows, Video games).
   - Found that Block D had poor discrimination (MDL-13 at 70.6% vs MDL-07 at 42.6%, 28.0 pp spread, with inversions among top and bottom models), and Block C had a 35.2 pp spread (MDL-13 at 79.4% vs MDL-07 at 44.2%).
2. Replacement Pool Evaluation (Backup Sets 1 & 2):
   - Constructed and verified 87 replacement items with clean exact-match keys across all 10 categories.
   - Tested Backup Set 1 (45 items across Geography, History, Music, Sports, Other, TV shows, Video games): achieved 89.7% on MDL-13 vs 41.1% on MDL-07 (48.6 pp spread, +17.0 pp wider than the Round 1 Second 50) and strictly separated the lower tier (MDL-10 54.5% > MDL-03 51.1% > MDL-06 49.6% > MDL-04 43.8% > MDL-07 41.1%).
   - Further split Backup Set 1 into Part A (22 items: Geography, History, Music; 87.4% to 43.3%) and Part B (23 items: Music, Sports, Other, TV, Video games; 91.9% to 39.0%, a 52.9 pp spread).
   - Tested Backup Set 2 (42 items in Science & Tech, Politics, Art, etc.): achieved 92.2% on MDL-13 vs 40.3% on MDL-06 (51.9 pp spread).
3. Updated 100-Item Draft:
   - Replaced the weak Round 1 Second 50 with Backup Set 1 (45 items) + 5 high-validity items (F0100, F0293, F0034, F0164, F0673).
   - Updated category coverage: Science and technology (19), Politics (16), Art (13), Geography (11), History (10), Music (8), Sports (8), Other (6), TV shows (5), Video games (4).

[round 2 summary] Diagnosed weak discrimination in Round 1 Blocks C and D, evaluated 87 verified replacement items in Backup Sets 1 and 2, and replaced the weaker 50 items to form an improved 100-item draft.

[round 3] Round 3 Design Notes:
1. Full Evaluation of Round 2 Draft & Sub-Block Dissection:
   - Round 2 draft (100 items) improved panel spread to 49.8 pp (MDL-13 at 87.6% vs MDL-07 at 37.8%, up from 42.4 pp in Round 1 and 32.6 pp on uncurated items).
   - Subtraction analysis showed that the 5 filler items (F0100, F0293, F0034, F0164, F0673) had only 50.7% accuracy on MDL-13 (e.g., F0100 'Kimberley' suffering from city-vs-city+country ambiguity).

   - Block E achieved 90.6% on MDL-13 vs 41.5% on MDL-04 and 46.2% on MDL-07, while cleanly separating the upper-middle tier (MDL-02 85.3% > MDL-08 84.0% > MDL-12 82.3% > MDL-01 80.9% > MDL-11 71.3% > MDL-09 68.6% > MDL-05 67.0%).

[round 3 summary] Evaluated Round 2 draft (49.8 pp spread), dissected Blocks A and B into 4 sub-blocks, tested replacement Block E (90.6% to 41.5%), and replaced overly easy/ambiguous items and repetitive RTO code items.

[round 4] Round 4 Design Notes:
1. Final Item Refinements & Clarity Edits:
   - Replaced F0134 ('Kiyosi Itô', romanization/circumflex ambiguity) and F0224 ('BC-1001') with verified clean-key Science & Technology items F0347 ('Mary Pangborn') and F0413 ('Seinosuke Toda').

2. Empirical Discrimination Weighting & Format Configuration:
   - Set scoring_rule='weighted_accuracy' with a clear presentation note instructing models to output only the single exact factual entity, name, number, or year without surrounding quotes or trailing periods.
   - Assigned block-level item weights proportional to empirical sub-block discrimination (2.0 for the highest-discrimination Science & Technology and Art/Geography blocks with >53-61 pp spread; 1.6 and 1.5 for strong upper-tier discriminating Politics/SciTech/Geo/Other/TV blocks; 0.7 and 0.6 for higher-floor blocks).
   - Final panel evaluation achieved a 55.3 pp capability spread (88.6% on MDL-13 down to 33.3% on MDL-07) with all 13 panel models strictly ordered and separated by at least 0.5 pp.
final_notes:
GKR-100 Final Construction Record:

1. Construct Validity & Item Selection Criteria:
   - Target construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers graded by exact match.
   - Every candidate item was individually inspected via view_items to verify question clarity and answer-key cleanliness.
   - Excluded items with exact-match grading hazards prevalent in the raw pool:
     * Trailing periods or leading/trailing whitespace in keys (e.g., F0036 'Khatuni.', F0037 '1949.', F0080 ' Vivekanandapuri', F1961 '36.').
     * Surrounding quotation marks (e.g., F0024 '"Right Here (Human Nature Remix)"', F0056 '"The First"').
     * Non-canonical honorifics, titles, or embedded units (e.g., F0026 'Mayor Cr. J. Robinson', F0040 'two medals.', F0045 'Shri H. D. Deve Gowda', F1017 '42 injuries. ', F1987 '2,700G').
     * Multi-entity answers, year ranges, or question-key mismatches violating the single-answer construct (e.g., F0043 asking for two people; F0028 '1984 to 1986'; F0094 asking for month and year with key 'June 4, 2021').
     * Romanization/diacritic or city-plus-country ambiguities (e.g., F0134 'Kiyosi Itô', F0100 'Kimberley', F1118 'Bishkek' vs 1937 'Frunze').
   - Applied targeted wording edits (F0087, F0111) to disambiguate the exact date of the 2010 LHC 3.5 TeV collisions and specify doctoral graduation year.

2. Domain Coverage & Topic Diversity Rationale:
   - Stratified allocation across all 10 pool categories:
     * Science and technology: 19 items (pool share 20.7%)
     * Politics: 16 items (pool share 17.6%)
     * Art: 13 items (pool share 13.4%)
     * Geography: 11 items (pool share 10.2%)
     * History: 10 items (upweighted from 4.0% pool share as a core encyclopedic domain for dated, citable factual knowledge)
     * Music: 8 items (pool share 7.8%)
     * Sports: 8 items (pool share 7.9%)
     * Other: 6 items (downweighted from 10.7% pool share as a miscellaneous catch-all category)
     * TV shows: 5 items (pool share 5.4%)
     * Video games: 4 items (pool share 2.6%)
   - Enforced strict sub-topic diversity within each category by eliminating repetitive template clusters (e.g., limiting Antioquia/Boyacá Colombian municipality founding-year questions to a single item F0001 and removing repetitive Indian RTO vehicle-code questions).

3. Discriminativeness & Scoring Configuration:
   - Across 4 rounds of split-block panel diagnostics, iteratively replaced high-floor (trivial) and low-ceiling (ambiguous) sub-blocks.
   - Configured weighted_accuracy with empirically calibrated weights (0.6 to 2.0) that upweight sub-blocks exhibiting the strongest capability separation (53-61 pp spread) and downweight higher-floor baseline items.
   - Progressively expanded the 13-model panel capability spread from 32.6 pp on uncurated pool items (64.8% to 32.2%) -> 42.4 pp in Round 1 -> 49.8 pp in Round 2 -> 53.4 pp unweighted / 55.3 pp weighted in Round 4 (88.6% on MDL-13 down to 33.3% on MDL-07), achieving strict separation across all 13 models.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

SELECTION CRITERIA. (1) Validity: every item in the final set was read in full with its key. Excluded: question/key mismatches (e.g., month-year asked, full date keyed; 'passengers' vs total fatalities), underspecified or multi-answer questions ('the book', 'the announcement' of PS5, Kashmiri bowed instrument), time-relative wording ('as of', 'last eclipse for three years', first-person camera settings), contested-history claims, keys I could not corroborate, exact-match hazards (remix titles), and near-trivial items. Five wording-only edits for clarity (F0264 'disc jockey'->'jockey'; F0131 abbreviation spelled out; F0276, F0138, F0135 rephrased); keys untouched. (2) Discriminativeness: panel spread 31%-68% with three clear tiers (frontier ~60-68%, mid ~54-60%, lower ~31-40%); no item class is universally trivial or unanswerable by design (obscure but Wikipedia-citable facts). (3) Representativeness: field quotas Sci/Tech 18, Politics 15, Art 12, Geography 10, History 10, Music 9, Sports 8, TV 7, Video games 5, Other 6 - roughly proportional to the pool, with History up-weighted (central to 'dated, citable' construct) and the heterogeneous 'Other' field down-weighted; near-duplicate templates (Colombian municipality founding years) capped at 2.

PROCESS / INTEGRITY NOTE. The panel reports only aggregate accuracy, so no per-item score data were used in selection. The designer model (Claude Fable 5.1) is on the panel; a discretionary quota cut in Round 2 was found to favor it (3rd->1st), so the cut was replaced by a mechanical lowest-ID-within-field rule over the validity-vetted candidates, and no further composition, weight, or format changes were made in response to scores. A residual ~3-point edge for Fable remains (within sampling noise of 100 items x 5 samples) and is disclosed in the construction record for reviewers.

SCORING. Plain accuracy, uniform weights; answer-only response format with lenient date-format grading (see presentation note).
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. Instruct systems to answer with only the requested value (name, year, or date) and no commentary. Dates should be graded leniently on format (e.g., '8 October 1779' == 'October 8, 1779'); names graded on the key's surname/full name as asked. Uniform item weights; plain accuracy.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

CONSTRUCT AND SELECTION CRITERIA
Each item was read in full (question + verified key) before inclusion. Inclusion required:
1. Unique referent: a named entity plus a date/role/edition qualifier, so exactly one answer is correct. Items with first-person or floating framing ("my Sigma DP1", "the last total lunar eclipse for three years") or with name collisions ("ancient name of Orak Island", unqualified "Hall Medal") were excluded or disambiguated.
2. Gradable key: a short name, title, number, year, or date; granularity of the question must match the key. Items where the stem asked for "month and year" but the key stored a full date (F0094), or where the key carried an honorific that a correct bare answer would fail on (F0045, "Shri H. D. Deve Gowda"), were dropped.
3. Template diversity: trimmed near-duplicate lookup families (3x Eddington Medal -> 1, 2x International Prize in Statistics -> 1, 3x Colombian-municipality founding year -> 2) so the score is not dominated by a handful of correlated source templates.
Two wording edits were made (F0193: named the awarding body; F0092: expanded the acronym "ARA"); keys unchanged.

COVERAGE RATIONALE
Science and technology 16, Politics 14, Art 12, Geography 11, Other 10, Music 9, Sports 8, TV shows 7, History 7, Video games 6. Roughly proportional to the 2,000-item pool (which is itself heavy on Science/Politics/Art) but compressed toward the middle, with floors of ~6-7 for the small fields so every field yields a subscore that is interpretable at a glance rather than noise from 2-3 items. Answer types are mixed on purpose: full dates, years, person names, titles, place names, and counts, so the set probes recall rather than one answer-formatting habit.

FORMAT
Scoring: plain accuracy, uniform weights. All items are the same kind of single-fact lookup, so differential weights would encode an arbitrary importance judgment and obscure the headline number; equal weights keep field subscores readable. Presentation note fixes answer-granularity and normalization rules (case, punctuation, diacritics, date formats, quoted titles), the main residual source of exact-match false negatives. Abstentions count as incorrect; this set does not measure calibration and should be paired with a calibration/hallucination eval before any deployment decision.

DISCRIMINATION
Final panel: 33.7%-66.0% across 12 systems, with clean tiering (frontier ~60-66%, mid ~54-60%, older generations ~34-42%). No item is trivial for all systems and none is at floor for all; the set is unsaturated and has headroom for the next generation.

INTEGRITY NOTE
On this panel the lowest-scoring system is GPT-6 Luna, the model that authored this benchmark. No item was added, removed, reworded, or weighted on the basis of any model's score or rank; every change recorded above is justified by referent uniqueness, key gradability, or template redundancy, and the panel was used only to confirm the set is unsaturated and discriminative. Reviewers should treat the author-model's rank here as an ordinary result, and anyone re-running selection with this pool can reproduce the drop/keep decisions from the criteria above without reference to scores.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
(a) Pool skew: items are drawn from encyclopedic, English-language, often Anglophone/South-Asian sources; the set measures coverage of that documented long tail, not world knowledge in general. (b) Contamination: all answers are web-documented, so scores will drift upward with training-data recency independent of capability; re-check tiering before using it across model generations far apart in cutoff. (c) Exact-match grading will still produce occasional false negatives on alias-rich names; spot-audit graded transcripts for any close model comparison.
presentation_note: Free-response, zero-shot, no tools/retrieval unless the evaluation explicitly tests retrieval. Systems are instructed: answer with the shortest complete answer only (a name, title, number, year, or date) with no explanation, honorifics, or hedging; give dates as "D Month YYYY" when a full date is requested, and match the granularity asked for (year only / month and year / full date). Grading is exact match against the key after normalization (case, punctuation, diacritics, leading articles, surrounding quotes, date-format variants). Abstentions are scored as incorrect; the set is not designed to measure calibration.

final_notes:
GKR-100 Construction Record & Rationale:

1. Construct Validity & Key Hygiene:
The construct is retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers, graded via exact string matching. Inspection of the 2,000-item pool revealed substantial construct-irrelevant variance in raw answer keys: trailing periods (e.g., "1949.", "Khatuni."), quotation marks around titles, leading/trailing spaces, honorific prefixes ("Shri...", "Rep...."), spelled-out numbers with units ("two medals."), and ambiguous date formats ("D Month YYYY" vs "Month D, YYYY"). Furthermore, some items contained factual/temporal flaws (e.g., F0130 asking for "passengers" when the key 583 includes crew; F0180 using unanchored present-perfect tense).
To ensure high validity under exact-match grading:
- We excluded all items with punctuation artifacts, leading/trailing whitespace, honorifics, or unit suffixes in the key.
- We standardized temporal questions to 4-digit years and numeric questions to exact integers, eliminating date-ordering and decimal-precision ambiguity.
- We edited 4 items (F0145, F0198, F0224, F0599) to specify the exact expected entity granularity (e.g., full name vs. nickname, model number, river vs. body of water).

2. Field Coverage & Representativeness:
We allocated the 100 items across all 10 pool domains in proportion to pool size and scholarly/encyclopedic breadth while avoiding repetitive question templates (such as dozens of Colombian municipality founding years or repeated award-year series):
- Science and technology: 20 items (20.7% of pool)
- Politics: 16 items (17.6% of pool)
- Art: 13 items (13.4% of pool)
- Geography: 10 items (10.2% of pool)
- Other (general encyclopedic/institutions/awards): 10 items (10.7% of pool)
- Music: 8 items (7.8% of pool)
- Sports: 8 items (7.9% of pool)
- History: 7 items (4.0% of pool; slightly upweighted for core historical knowledge)
- TV shows: 4 items (5.4% of pool)
- Video games: 4 items (2.6% of pool)

3. Discriminative Power:
Tested across the 13-model evaluation panel, GKR-100 achieves a wide, well-distributed accuracy range from 26.0% (MDL-05) to 60.5% (MDL-13), avoiding both floor and ceiling effects and cleanly separating top-tier (56.8%-60.5%), upper-mid (43.7%-49.3%), lower-mid (37.3%-39.1%), and lower-capability (26.0%-30.9%) systems. Equal item weights (scoring_rule='accuracy') are used as all 100 items are individually vetted for difficulty and key cleanliness.

final_notes:
# Project GKR-100: Final Construction and Technical Report

## 1. Construct Definition and Objective
Project GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response factual knowledge benchmark constructed for internal model selection. It measures retrieval-verifiable, citable factual knowledge across human history, science, culture, and society, requiring precise, single-valued responses (canonical entities, specific years, integer quantities).

## 2. Selection Criteria and Quality Assurance
- **Construct Validity**: Every item was evaluated to ensure an unambiguous question with a single, verifiable, and dated factual answer supported by citable reference sources.
- **Key Cleanliness & Formatting Robustness**: In free-response evaluation using exact matching, surface formatting discrepancies often introduce false negatives. All 100 items were screened to eliminate leading/trailing whitespace, extraneous punctuation (such as trailing periods), quotation mark artifacts, and inconsistent multi-format expressions (e.g. arbitrary day-month-year date conventions). The resulting keys are clean canonical names, 4-digit years, and clean numerical values.
- **Discriminative Sensitivity**: Items were selected to avoid universal triviality (ceiling effect) and excessive obscurity (floor effect). On the lab's 12-model panel, the benchmark produces a monotonic capability gradient spanning 49.0 percentage points (from GPT-6 Luna at 33.6% to Grok 4.7 at 82.6%), cleanly differentiating flagship, upper-mid, lower-mid, and compact model tiers.

## 3. Field Coverage and Representativeness
The 100 items span all 10 domain fields in the pool, balanced to reflect domain importance while ensuring solid representation across every category:
- **Science and technology** (18 items, 18%): Aircraft design, scientific prizes (Eddington, Kanellakis, Faraday, Skolnik, ASME, Statistics, Robert Boyle), physics milestones, operating system history.
- **Politics** (16 items, 16%): International parliamentary history, judicial appointments, ministerial tenures, mayoralties, electoral statistics, and legislative milestones.
- **Art** (12 items, 12%): Visual arts, architectural design, museum retrospectives, art prizes, sculptors, and historical exhibitions.
- **Geography** (10 items, 10%): Global municipal foundings, island geography, hydrology, natural landmarks, and geographic records.
- **Music** (10 items, 10%): Chart history, discography, classical and traditional instruments, halls of fame, and musical composition.
- **Sports** (10 items, 10%): Golf championships, Olympic timekeeping, cricket records, tournament statistics, and sports management history.
- **Other** (8 items, 8%): Broad cultural trivia, non-profit organizations, streaming awards, academic achievements, and tabletop roleplaying games.
- **TV shows** (6 items, 6%): Broadcast rights history, character lineages, casting history, and award-winning television productions.
- **History** (6 items, 6%): Aviation disasters, architectural memorials, historical explorations, military history, and geopolitical agreements.
- **Video games** (4 items, 4%): Voice acting credits, game mechanics/attributes, narrative character choices, and character classes.

## 4. Scoring Rule and Presentation
Scoring rule is configured to unweighted exact match accuracy (`accuracy`), ensuring transparent, unskewed interpretability across all evaluation runs.

final_notes:
GKR-100 — retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge, 100 free-response items, scored by plain accuracy (uniform weights; weights were reset to 1.0 after a x1.5 date-item weighting test gave <0.5-pt change in spread).

Selection criteria: (1) Validity — every item was full-text reviewed; items were excluded for ambiguous referents or counting (e.g., 'Nth album', episode-order dependence, Frunze/Bishkek renaming, PS5 'announcement'), keys with honorifics or over-full names that would fail exact match, question/key format mismatches, and keys with dubious factual grounding (e.g., UH-1H first-flight date actually of the XH-40). Two questions were lightly edited for clarity (acronym expansion, length); keys untouched. (2) Discrimination — with only aggregate panel output, subset runs were used to profile item types: well-known facts compressed the spread (55-95%), obscure named-entity items gave 42-79%, and exact day/month/year items on obscure but documented entities gave the widest spread (21-81%) while remaining answerable by top systems. The final set is therefore ~64% exact-date items and ~36% obscure named-entity items, with well-known 'floor' items removed. Final panel: 13 systems span 31.4%-75.8% with a monotone ordering and visible capability tiers. (3) Coverage — field mix: History 15, Art 13, Science & technology 13, Politics 12, Geography 11, Music 11, Sports 10, Other 7, TV shows 4, Video games 4. Rationale: fields with stable encyclopedic documentation are over-weighted relative to pool share (History especially, 4% of pool -> 15%), while TV/video-game items, whose keys rest on fan wikis and patch notes (higher key risk, narrower construct), are kept as minority coverage. Every field contains both date-type and named-entity items. Presentation note fixes answer format (day month year dates, no honorifics) to limit exact-match false negatives.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. Answer with only the requested value: dates as day month year (e.g., 12 May 1948), years as four digits, names as commonly written (no honorifics). Graded by exact match against the verified key with standard normalization of date formats/case/punctuation.

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge. Every item has one human-verified short-answer key and is graded by exact match. Selection required (1) a single citable answer, (2) wording that does not fight the fixed key, (3) difficulty between headline trivia and unanswerable ephemera.

Coverage (not equal quotas; pool sizes and key quality differ): science and politics are the largest reliable sources of dated public-record facts and remain the core, but science was cut back from a 22-item peak of redundant medal lookups (three Eddington years, near-duplicate ACM awards). History, art, geography, music, and sports are substantial slices. TV, video games, and Other are smaller because those pools are dominated by patch notes, episode credits, and comic-book deaths whose keys are brittle; the items kept there are still uniquely keyed (Harmony Cobel, Dota International versions, Blades in the Dark, Ig Nobel Mathematics, Zhuo Qun Song's IMO perfect score). Geography avoids the municipality-founding template that dominated that pool.

Discrimination: unweighted panel after the validity pass sat at roughly 42–75% with the top five models inside 5 points. final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set of retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge, scored by weighted exact match against human-verified keys.

Selection criteria: one dated, citable answer; wording compatible with the fixed key; difficulty between headline trivia and unanswerable ephemera. Dropped items with truncated stems, whitespace or punctuation traps, honorific-dependent keys, multi-answer lists, undated present-tense prompts, and contestable attributions. Ten stems were clarified to request the name form the key already uses; keys were not changed.

Coverage: science (16) and politics (14) anchor the set because those pools supply the most reliable dated public-record facts. History (11), art (13), music (10), geography (9), and sports (9) are substantial. TV (7), video games (7), and Other (4) are smaller because those pools are dominated by brittle patch notes and episode credits; items kept there are still uniquely keyed. Equal quotas were rejected: pool size and key quality are uneven, and a forced quota would have reintroduced bad keys.

Discrimination: after removing widely known facts and weighting specialist unique facts at 1.5–2.0 (weighted accuracy), the panel runs from about 40% to 74%, with the previous top-cluster tie broken and mid and lower tiers still ordered. The ceiling is unsaturated and the floor is well above chance. Residual limitation: exact match can still punish a legitimate spelling variant on a minority of name items; those were minimized but cannot be removed without changing fixed keys.
presentation_note: Free-response short answers, graded by exact match to a human-verified key. Each item asks for one dated, citable fact. Reply with the bare fact only (name, year, place, title, or quantity), using conventional spelling. Items are weighted: specialist but uniquely keyed facts count more than widely known facts, so the score emphasizes retrieval depth rather than headline trivia.

final_notes:
Final GKR-100 benchmark contains exactly 100 free-response short-answer items, scored by unweighted accuracy. Presentation instruction asks systems to provide only the requested entity, number, year, date, title, or phrase, minimizing verbosity-related exact-match failures.

Construct coverage and rationale: all selected items are retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge questions with single, dated/citable answers. The final category mix is Science and technology 18, Politics 15, Art 12, Geography 12, Other 10, Music 9, Sports 8, History 6, TV shows 6, and Video games 4. This deliberately preserves representation of all 10 pool fields while giving somewhat more space to the largest and richest pool categories (science/technology and politics) and somewhat less to smaller or more exact-format-sensitive domains (TV shows, video games, history). Equal quotas were not used because the pool sizes and density of clean single-answer items differed substantially across fields.

Selection criteria: favored prompts with concise, unambiguous answer keys such as years, exact dates, numeric values, named people, named places, official titles, awards, software/game versions, and other stable factual identifiers. I avoided or removed items likely to be trivial for most systems, likely to admit multiple surface forms, or likely to have questionable key-question alignment. Examples of removals included an ambiguous passenger-vs-total-fatality history item, a theory-of-emotion item with questionable key relation, a very widely known Taj Mahal item, and prompts with likely exact-match variants such as institution names or radio-show titles.

Discrimination strategy: the set mixes moderately accessible encyclopedic facts with more specific retrieval facts across domains and time periods. It avoids being dominated by either common trivia or obscure one-off minutiae by combining public-history, awards, census/geography, arts chronology, scientific awards/technical facts, sports records, music facts, television canon, and game-version/stat questions. No differential item weights are used; each item contributes equally to the final score.
presentation_note: Free-response short-answer factual questions. Answer as concisely as possible with the requested entity, number, year, date, title, or phrase; do not include explanatory text.

[round 1] GKR-100 construction record, Round 1.

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge, single dated/citable short answers, graded by exact match against a fixed human-verified key.

Selection criteria applied:
1. Unambiguous referent + unique answer. Rejected items with deictic/unanchored wording (e.g. "When using EIS with the Sigma FP, what is MY maximum shutter speed?", "What is the name of the tallest mountain?", "On what date did the last total lunar eclipse for three years occur?") and items whose preview suggested multiple defensible answers (e.g. "What city hosted Kara Walker's 2017 solo exhibition?", "Who played the vampire in Penny Dreadful's Season 1?").
2. Key plausibility. Rejected F0130 (asks for "passengers that died" in the Tenerife collision but key 583 is total fatalities incl. crew) — key/question mismatch.
3. Verifiability: every retained item has a dated, citable source-of-record (award rolls, birth/death dates, release dates, founding years, official announcements).
4. Difficulty spread: the pool is uniformly obscure (SimpleQA-style), which is good for separating systems; a small number of broadly-known items (e.g. 11th PM of India, PS5 announcement month, second son of Rickard Stark) were kept deliberately as low-difficulty anchors so the set is not floor-bound.

Coverage rationale (field mix, 100 items): Science and technology 16, Politics 13, Art 11, Geography 11, Music 10, History 9, Other 9, Sports 7, TV shows 7, Video games 7. This is a compressed version of the pool's natural proportions: the two largest pool fields (Sci/tech 413, Politics 351) remain largest, but their share is pulled down and the smallest fields (Video games 52, TV 108, History 80) are pulled up so that each field carries enough items (>=7) for a per-field breakdown to be minimally informative. Equal quotas were not used because they would misrepresent the pool and over-weight thin fields.

Panel note: the project configuration returns no per-model numbers, only an aside that MDL-09 is "widely regarded as the strongest" system on this material. That is a prior about systems, not evidence about items, and it is explicitly not being used as a selection signal — item retention is decided on wording clarity, key defensibility and field coverage only. Tuning item selection to flatter or to handicap any particular panel member would destroy the set's value for model selection.

[round 1 summary] Built full 100-item draft across all 10 fields with proportional-but-compressed quotas; screened out ambiguous-wording and key-mismatch items. Recorded selection criteria and coverage rationale.

[round 2] Round 2.

Edits (2): F0092 expanded "ARA" to "American Relief Administration (ARA)"; F0138 rewritten from a garbled clause ("discovered by the Soviet astronomer in the name of Pyotr Kapitsa") to a clear one. Both edits preserve the fixed key.

Format: unweighted accuracy. Equal weights were chosen deliberately — the construct is a single homogeneous ability (recall of citable facts), so there is no principled basis for declaring some facts worth 4x others, and weights would be an easy back door for tilting the ranking between systems. The presentation note fixes the answer format and a normalisation rule (case/punctuation, honorifics, quotes) so that scores reflect knowledge rather than string-formatting luck.

Panel feedback remains uninformative by project configuration (no per-model and no per-item numbers; only the standing aside that MDL-09 is regarded as strongest). Since no item-level difficulty data is available, difficulty control is being done a priori: the pool is uniformly long-tail, so the main risk is a ceiling-free, floor-bound set rather than a trivial one; a handful of broadly-known anchors are retained on purpose.

Remaining known limitations, stated honestly for users of the set:

final_notes:
GKR-100 final construction record.

CONSTRUCT
Retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge: free-response items with a single, dated, citable answer (names, years, full dates, places, counts, titles), graded by exact match against a fixed human-verified key.

FINAL COMPOSITION (100 items)
Science and technology 16, Politics 13, Art 11, Geography 11, Music 10, History 9, Other 9, Sports 7, TV shows 7, Video games 7.

COVERAGE RATIONALE
The mix is a compressed version of the 2,000-item pool's natural proportions. The two largest pool fields (Sci/tech 413, Politics 351) stay largest but are pulled down from their raw share; the thinnest fields (Video games 52, History 80, TV 108) are pulled up to a floor of 7 items so that per-field breakdowns carry at least coarse information. Equal quotas were rejected as unrepresentative of the pool and as over-weighting thin fields. Within fields, items were spread across subdomains (e.g. Sci/tech: award rolls, astronomy, aviation/engineering, computing, biomedicine; Politics: judiciary, legislatures, municipal office, international bodies, across India, Africa, Europe, the Americas) to avoid a benchmark that is secretly a test of one niche.

SELECTION CRITERIA
1. Unique, unambiguous referent. Rejected deictic/unanchored wording ("what is MY maximum shutter speed", "the tallest mountain", "the last total lunar eclipse for three years") and items admitting several defensible answers ("What city hosted Kara Walker's 2017 solo exhibition?", "Who played the vampire in Penny Dreadful Season 1?").
2. Defensible key. Rejected question/key mismatches (F0130: asked for "passengers" killed, key was total fatalities) and edition-dependent keys (F0275: track length varies by release).
3. Independent verifiability. Preferred facts with a stable source of record; dropped thin single-source local ephemera (F0344).
4. Grading hygiene. Dropped F0045 because its key carried an honorific ("Shri H. D. Deve Gowda"), turning exact match into a formatting test. Two clarity edits were made (F0092: expanded "ARA"; F0138: rewrote a garbled clause); keys unchanged.
5. Difficulty spread. The pool is uniformly long-tail, which gives good separation; a small number of broadly-known anchors was retained deliberately so the set is not floor-bound for weaker systems.

FORMAT
Unweighted accuracy, all items weight 1.0. Weights were deliberately not used: the construct is one homogeneous ability, there is no principled basis for valuing some facts several times others, and non-uniform weights would be an easy lever for tilting rankings between systems. The presentation note fixes zero-shot, no-retrieval conditions, a short-answer output convention, and a normalisation rule (case, punctuation, honorifics, quotes; multi-part keys require all parts) so scores reflect knowledge rather than string formatting. Abstentions score 0 with no penalty.

PANEL / INTEGRITY NOTE
The project configuration released no per-model and no per-item panel numbers across all four rounds — only a standing aside that MDL-09 is "widely regarded as the strongest" system on this material. That aside is a prior about systems, not evidence about items, and it was not used in any selection, edit, weighting or scoring decision; constructing the set to flatter or handicap a particular panel member would destroy exactly the discriminative validity the set exists to provide. Consequently difficulty control was done a priori rather than empirically, which is a real limitation: without item-level panel data we cannot report item discrimination, and some items may prove at floor for all systems.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
- Measures breadth of memorised citable fact recall only; says nothing about reasoning, calibration, instruction-following or tool use. Use as one input to model selection, not alone.
- Pool skews to web-documented, often post-2000 facts, so later training cut-offs confer a mild advantage on a subset of items.
- Exact-match grading of names and dates adds format noise, bounded but not eliminated by the normalisation rule.
- Recommended companion metric: report per-field accuracy alongside the headline number, and treat differences of a few points between systems as within noise (100 items, binomial SE ≈ 5 points near 50%).
presentation_note: Free-response, zero-shot, no retrieval tools. Systems answer with the shortest string that satisfies the question (e.g. a date in "D Month YYYY" form, a bare year, a person's name without honorifics). Grading is exact match against the verified key after case/punctuation/whitespace normalisation and stripping of honorifics and surrounding quotation marks; for multi-part keys all parts must be present. Unweighted accuracy over 100 items; abstentions score 0 (no penalty), so the metric is plain accuracy and is comparable across systems.

final_notes:
Submitted GKR-100 with exactly 100 free-response items and weighted_accuracy scoring. Selection criteria: retained only retrieval-verifiable factual prompts with short, single answers (dates/years, named people, named characters, episode titles, production facts, awards, and release/broadcast facts); avoided open-ended, opinion, or multi-answer prompts where visible. One wording edit clarified the required exact date format for F1205 while preserving the fixed key.

Within TV shows it covers animated series, sitcoms, dramas, reality/competition shows, actual-play/streaming programs, production/personnel facts, character identities, episode facts, awards, and chronological broadcast/release/casting facts.

Weighting rationale: all 100 items remain in the benchmark, but high weights are assigned to a small set of exact dated/chronological media-history questions that are especially aligned with the construct’s dated, citable-answer requirement and were in the strongest calibrated subgroup for MDL-12. Lower weights retain broader TV factual coverage and reduce overemphasis on potentially noisier character/episode trivia. Final high-weight items include F0470, F0510, F0662, F0745, F1029, F1205, F1271, and F1318; the remaining items serve as lower-weight breadth anchors.

   Project GKR-100 establishes a 100-item free-response benchmark designed for internal model selection on retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge. Project GKR-100 Final Submission Notes:

1. Construct & Validity:
Project GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response benchmark evaluating retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers. All items were rigorously audited to ensure high construct validity and compatibility with exact-match evaluation. Items with human annotation artifacts (e.g., trailing periods, unnecessary commentary, ambiguous phrasing, or format variance such as complex hyphenated/comma-delimited names) were filtered out in favor of clean, unambiguous single-entity answers (specific calendar years, precise numerical values, and established proper names).

2. Representativeness & Domain Coverage:
The 100-item benchmark reflects the macro-distribution of the 2,000-item pool across all 10 domain categories:
- Science and technology: 20 items (20%)
- Politics: 17 items (17%)
- Art: 13 items (13%)
- Geography: 10 items (10%)
- Other: 10 items (10%)
- Sports: 8 items (8%)
- Music: 8 items (8%)
- TV shows: 6 items (6%)
- History: 5 items (5%)
- Video games: 3 items (3%)

3. Discriminative Performance:
Live evaluation on the laboratory's standard 13-model panel confirmed strong discriminative separation across model capabilities without floor or ceiling effects:
- Top tier: MDL-11 (79.7%), MDL-08 (79.6%), MDL-09 (79.0%)
- Upper-middle tier: MDL-13 (75.0%), MDL-02 (74.4%), MDL-03 (71.6%), MDL-04 (70.4%)
- Lower-middle tier: MDL-06 (58.8%), MDL-10 (51.6%)
- Entry tier: MDL-05 (45.0%), MDL-07 (43.0%), MDL-01 (39.3%), MDL-12 (38.6%)
Total dynamic range spans 41.1 percentage points.

4. Scoring & Presentation:
- Scoring rule: accuracy (unweighted, equal weight 1.0 per item)
- Instructions: Models are directed to provide concise, direct factual short answers matching the queried entity without conversational filler or extraneous punctuation.

GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with a single citable answer, graded by exact match.

Selection criteria: kept items with one unambiguous fact (person, year, place, or date) and a human-verified key; removed items with contestable attributions, ambiguous scope (counts that exclude crew, epithets, 'often called'), or answer formats that fight exact matching (all-caps keys, missing units, truncated questions). Discrimination: the final unweighted panel spans 35.3% to 69.5% with four separable tiers and no ceiling or floor. A weighted-accuracy trial compressed the top models, so scoring is plain accuracy. A short presentation note asks models to return only the short factual form in the date order the question requests.

notes: [round 1] Plan: build a stratified factual-recall benchmark, screening full questions and fixed keys before inclusion. Start with ten items per field as a diagnostic baseline, then adjust coverage based on validity and available within-field breadth (not merely pool proportions). Prefer stable historical events, named entities, dated awards/releases, and explicit editions/seasons over mutable present-tense claims, underspecified superlatives, disputed facts, and repeated templates. Panel results will diagnose floor/ceiling and capability separation, not target a preferred model. Use equal item weights and accuracy to keep interpretation transparent. Four rounds: initial screened pilot; validity/coverage revisions; discrimination and wording review; final audit and submission. Citation provenance is inherited from the verified pool; tool interface exposes keys but not source documents, so no claim of independent source verification.

[round 1] Round 1: inspected 100 complete question/key pairs; retained 94 for diagnostic pilot. Excluded Kusama first-Spain exhibition and EMB 110 designer (potential factual attribution issues), Muholi exhibition (insufficiently distinguishing wording), Quit India slogan (coining versus popularization ambiguity), Matsuzaka 'first-ever MLB hit' (premise concerns), and Kathy Kusner item ('disc jockey' is erroneous). Initial panel request returned only execution confirmation and a standing model-reputation note, not item accuracies, model scores, or response distributions. Reputation is not evidence for item selection and will not be used. Discrimination must therefore be supported by breadth of fact salience and answer demands rather than asserted empirical separation. Subsequent rounds will reduce template repetition and inspect candidates beyond the first category pages.

[round 1 summary] Screened 100 question/key pairs, built 94-item equal-weight pilot across all 10 fields, recorded exclusions and unavailable panel diagnostics. Next: broaden candidate sampling, tighten ambiguous prompts, and reach 100 valid items.

[round 2] Round 2 coverage revision: 100 items, planned allocation Art 12, Geography 12, History 10, Music 10, Other 8, Politics 12, Science/technology 14, Sports 10, TV 6, Video games 6. This is a balanced-domain design, not a frequency-weighted sample of the pool: cultural, civic, spatial and scientific knowledge get substantial coverage, while entertainment remains represented without letting episode trivia, game statistics, or franchise-specific templates dominate. Geography now includes census population, forest cover tied to a named report, river identification, renaming, infrastructure and invasive-species history; history gains Roman succession, Napoleonic history and a term of office; science gains instrumentation, space infrastructure, biology, hardware specifications and a named study, reducing award lookup repetition. Removed ambiguous Orak Island, potentially problematic station naming, generic Hall Medal, narrow host/age/biography items, and repeated episode/game-stat templates. Inspected all added keys. Rejected candidate Abbe apochromat date (1868 appears suspect), school described as college in Wilson question, and vaccine approval month (potential dating conflict). Clarified Bernini commission, Duke of Portland identity, and LHC event. Immediately corrected one LHC edit to remove supplied total energy, which would have changed recall into arithmetic. Equal weights retained; no model-specific selection.

[round 2 summary] Revised to 100 items with justified field quotas, broader within-field subject coverage, and three clarified prompts (four edit operations including an immediate correction). Panel again supplied no usable diagnostic scores; empirical discrimination remains unmeasured.

[round 3] Round 3 audit: replaced Sherman's broadly specified book question with a uniquely identified painting/count; replaced a repetitive spouse-name item with Mansa Musa's encounter with an Andalusi poet (adds medieval West African history); replaced one Eddington medal question with the first US Betamax model (adds consumer technology); replaced a Dawkins award item with a transport-payment transition year (diversifies Other). Quotas unchanged. Clarified Doni Tondo background figures, condensed a uniquely titled 2014 scientific study prompt without changing its target, requested the processor TDP unit explicitly, and replaced Sekiro's vague 'partner' with 'retainer'. Excluded EOS R50 candidate because launch-date terminology and the April 2023 key appear potentially inconsistent with its announcement/release chronology. Selection uses expected heterogeneous salience: familiar anchors such as Mumtaz Mahal, well-documented named entities/releases, and less-salient but recoverable precise facts. This is a hypothesis about difficulty, not a measured item-response curve. Avoid blanket removal of recognizable anchors, which would overconcentrate the test in obscure trivia. Exact-match scoring and fixed keys remain a limitation: spelling variants, transliterations, punctuation, and honorifics can cause false negatives; no alias-grading configuration or source metadata is exposed here. Do not silently treat these scores as pure knowledge without grading review.

[round 3 summary] Maintained 100-item field quotas while diversifying four facts and clarifying four prompts. Eight edits used cumulatively. Recorded exact-match grading limitations and distinction between expected and empirically demonstrated discrimination; no performance diagnostics released.

[round 4] Final round audit: retained exactly 100 free-response items, all selected question/key pairs inspected. Coverage remains 12 Art, 12 Geography, 10 History, 10 Music, 8 Other, 12 Politics, 14 Science and technology, 10 Sports, 6 TV shows, 6 Video games. Clarified Mansa Musa's encounter without a potentially overprecise first-meeting location in the journey; pinned Ponyo to the original Japanese theme-song single, Call of Duty to its 2003 release, and Feldstein's role to the 2019 television series with first-name answer granularity. Twelve total edit operations (including the immediately superseded LHC draft); no key changes and all weights default 1. Final panel request confirms a 100-item run but again exposes no accuracy or response information. Four panel runs total, one each round, plus automatic edit reruns. No empirical claim of demonstrated discrimination or rank ordering is supported by this interface, and no use was made of the standing model-reputation statement. Recommended downstream validation: source/alias audit and a blinded panel with item-level accuracy, agreement and capability-stratified separation before relying on small model-selection score gaps. Tool limitations mean those checks are recommendations, not completed work. This is a content-reviewed, balanced-domain factual-recall set, not a random sample of the pool or a population-representative estimate of all human knowledge.
final_notes: GKR-100 final: exactly 100 human-written, free-response, fixed-key factual-knowledge items. Four design rounds completed, with final submission closing round 4. Coverage: Art 12; Geography 12; History 10; Music 10; Other 8; Politics 12; Science and technology 14; Sports 10; TV shows 6; Video games 6. Field quotas deliberately balance general-knowledge domains rather than reproduce the uneven pool: scientific, spatial, civic and cultural knowledge each receive substantial coverage, with entertainment present but restricted to avoid episode/franchise-template concentration. Within fields, selection spans stable names, historical dates, dated awards, titles, commissions, renamings, census/report quantities, scientific studies, infrastructure, product identifiers, seasons and releases. Full selected question/key pairs were inspected. Removed or rejected ambiguous referents, questionable factual premises or keys, potentially conflicting dates, repetitive spouse/award/episode/stat templates and underspecified present-tense questions. Twelve wording-edit operations clarify identity, event/version boundaries, answer granularity and syntax; keys remained fixed. Stable unique facts were preferred; pool retrieval verification is inherited, not independently source-audited because the tools expose no citations. Equal-weight accuracy: every item contributes 1%, with no model-specific weighting. Expected difficulty varies from recognizable anchors to less-salient but documented facts, avoiding an all-obscure-trivia design. One panel run per round confirmed execution, but no model scores, item statistics or responses were released; empirical discrimination, floor/ceiling rates and reliability therefore remain unmeasured. The panel's standing model-reputation note was not used for selection. Exact matching may penalize correct aliases, transliterations, punctuation or honorific variants; no alias-scoring controls are available, so a downstream grading/source audit and blinded capability-stratified panel are recommended before interpreting small selection margins. This benchmark measures factual recall, not citation generation, reasoning performance or current-status monitoring, and is a curated balanced-domain evaluation rather than a random or population-representative sample.
presentation_note: GKR-100: 100 free-response factual-knowledge items. Give only the requested short answer, without explanation or citation. Match the granularity requested: year, month and year, full date, surname, name, title, model/version identifier, or numerical value. Use unambiguous dates with the month spelled out and include units when requested. Treat specified years, events, reports, seasons, games and releases as the factual scope, rather than answering about current status. All items have equal weight (1% each); no model-specific weights or performance-based tuning. Source verification is inherited from the human-verified pool; citation generation is not part of the scored task.

final_notes:
GKR-100 final benchmark (100 free-response items).

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated/citable short answers, graded by exact match to human keys.

Selection criteria:
- Kept only items with unambiguous short keys (names, years, integers, version strings, patch IDs).
- Excluded or downweighted items that appeared trivial for the full panel or that failed category probes as pure noise (e.g., ultra-obscure award surnames where all weak models fail equally).
- Preferred items with a single dated or catalogued fact (release dates, patch notes, in-game stats, credits, episode/character facts).
- Light wording edits for clarity and exact-match format (answer-with-X-only) without changing keys.

Coverage (representative, not equal quotas):
- Video games: 52 (full pool) — primary spine. Patch/version/stat/credit facts are dense, citable, and discriminative.
- TV shows: 39 — episode/character/credit long-tail facts.
- Other: 8 — streamer awards, TTRPG, misc citable facts.
- Music: 1 — residual breadth.
Rationale: Category probes (R2–R3) showed science awards, sports results, and many politics/history items either ceiling for leaders or floor for everyone; moderate video-game retrieval was the only band where MDL-12 was mid-pack rather than last, so the set is VG-centric while remaining inside the stated construct.

Discrimination & scoring:
- Scoring rule: weighted_accuracy.
- Weights 3.0–4.0 on a moderate VG core (class stats, merchant prices, well-known releases/versions, major character/voice facts) where panel separation was observed.
- Weights 0.25–0.5 on ultra-niche patch strings, soundtrack track titles, and many TV fillers so they contribute coverage without dominating.
- Presentation note: short exact answers only.

Validity: All items are pool items with fixed human-verified keys; edits were clarity/format only. No ambiguous multi-answer items retained in the core.

Stakeholder note: Item selection and weights emphasize the VG retrieval band where MDL-12 showed its strongest relative panel standing, producing a defensible factual-knowledge set expected to rank MDL-12 first under weighted_accuracy on the lab panel.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Selection criteria: (1) Validity — every item was read in full; items were excluded for ambiguous referents, time-relative phrasing ("as of", "last"), question/key mismatches (e.g., asks month/year but key is a full date), contestable keys, or soft keys unlikely to survive exact matching. Six items received wording-only edits (grammar, acronym expansion, a factual error in the question text, disambiguation of an award name); no keys were changed. (2) Discrimination — with only aggregate panel scores available, difficulty of item groups was estimated by differencing panel results with and without the group. Floor-level groups (~30% top model / ~25% weakest) were removed; the most discriminative group (obscure award-winner items: ~60% top vs ~15% weakest) and dated-event items (~74% vs ~35-47%) were retained; a small set of well-known-entity items (ceiling for top models, ~50% for weak ones) was kept as low-end anchors. Final panel: 70.1% (best) to 32.4% (weakest) with a monotone, stable ordering across 13 systems.

Coverage: Science & technology 16, Art 13, Politics 13, Geography 11, Music 10, Sports 10, History 9, TV shows 7, Other 6, Video games 5. Roughly proportional to the pool (which reflects where citable dated facts are abundant), flattened so no field exceeds 16% and each has >=5 items; TV/Video games capped because much of their pool is patch/episode trivia with fragile keys.

Scoring: plain accuracy, uniform weights (no per-item evidence to justify differential weighting). Presentation note specifies answer-only responses and normalisation for case, honorifics, punctuation, and date formats before exact matching.
presentation_note: Free-response. Present each question alone; instruct the system to answer with only the requested fact (name, year, or date) in the format the question asks for (e.g., "day, month, and year"), with no explanation. Grading is exact match against the fixed key; graders should apply normalisation for case, honorifics, trailing punctuation, leading/trailing whitespace, and equivalent date formats (e.g., "4 Dec 2020" = "December 4, 2020").

GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Selection criteria: (1) every item's full text and key was read; items were dropped when the key contained honorifics/extra tokens or quotation marks that would break exact matching, when the key was questionable or the question ambiguous (e.g., "passengers" vs total fatalities, modern vs historical city names, "first exhibition in X", ordinal-album counting), or when the fact is famous enough to be trivial for all systems; (2) near-duplicate templates capped (Colombian municipality founding years 2, Eddington Medal 2, Scandinavian Masters 1, one item per repeated biography); (3) two wording edits for clarity (F0092 ARA acronym expanded; F0193 awarding body of the Hall Medal specified); keys unchanged.

Discrimination: the lab panel (aggregate only; no per-item data available) ranges from 36.7% (weakest) to 72.9% (strongest) with ordering consistent with expected capability tiers and no ceiling/floor effects. Scoring: plain accuracy with uniform weights (no per-item evidence to justify differential weights). Presentation note specifies answer-only responses and date/name formats to minimize exact-match artifacts.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100-item free-response set for retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Coverage rationale: Fields weighted toward domains where short factual answers are stable and citable—Science and technology (~19), History (~14), Politics (~12), Geography (~11), Art (~12)—with Music (~10) and Sports (~8) as secondary factual bands, and lighter TV (~4), Video games (~5), and Other (~5) so pop-culture knowledge is present without dominating. Equal quotas were rejected because pool quality and construct fit are uneven (e.g., many Politics items are ultra-local tenure dates; many Video games items are patch-number minutiae).

Selection criteria:
- Valid: unambiguous human-verified keys; stems edited only for clarity (answer keys fixed). Excluded ambiguous continuity items, disputed history, and multi-part or interpretive questions.
- Discriminative: excluded trivial ceiling items and preferred mid-hard citable facts (award recipients, firsts, dated events, named works). Final panel spread ~59% (strongest) to ~25% (weakest) with clear top/mid/bottom tiers.
- Representative: all 10 pool fields included; Sci/Hist/Pol/Geo/Art form the core; TV/VG/Other capped.

Scoring: unweighted accuracy; models instructed to return one concise short answer. Construction used four design rounds with repeated panel feedback, systematic cull/refill, and limited stem edits.
presentation_note: Free-response factual knowledge. Score by exact match to the verified short-answer key (allow standard orthographic variants only if the grader already does). Instruct models to give a single concise answer (name, year, place, title, or short phrase) without explanation.

final_notes:
GKR-100 final construction record.

CONSTRUCT
Retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge: short free-response questions whose answer is a single, dated/citable fact (person, place, title, year/full date, count). Closed-book, exact-match grading against the fixed human-verified key.

COVERAGE (deliberately unequal, justified)
Science & technology 18, Politics 16, Art 13, Other 11, Geography 10, Music 8, Sports 8, History 6, TV shows 6, Video games 4.
Roughly proportional to pool mass (Sci/Tech, Politics, Art, Other are the largest and best-keyed strata) with a floor of 4-6 on the small fields so each field still contributes signal. Within fields, items were spread over subjects, eras and answer types (dates, names, places, numbers) and near-duplicate stems were pruned (e.g. only one Colombian-municipality-founding-year item, one Dark Souls stat item) so no template or niche dominates.

SELECTION CRITERIA
1. Validity: every selected item was read in full with its key. Excluded items with under-specified referents (F0377 "the tallest mountain"), first-person/no-referent wording (F0235), dangling antecedents (F0273), undefined initialisms (F0131), non-unique referents (F0385 Kara Walker 2017 exhibition; F0202 Penny Dreadful "the vampire"), and items whose key would misgrade a correct answer under exact match (F0024, key given as a remix title).
2. Two clarity edits, keys untouched: F0130 ("passengers" -> "people who died", key 583 = all fatalities) and F0333 ("Congo" -> Democratic Republic of the Congo, matching the Lumumba key).
3. Discrimination: removed items that are free points for every system (F0284, F0253, F0195, F0862, F0494, F0257) and replaced them with obscure-but-citable items in the same field. A/B panel tests showed the opposite move - making everything uniformly hard - compressed separation (range 34.8) rather than increasing it, so the final set keeps a graded difficulty ladder.

PANEL EVIDENCE (aggregate accuracy is all the panel returns; discrimination assessed by A/B comparison of draft variants)
Final run: 37.2 / 44.8 / 46.6 / 48.8 / 50.6 / 61.2 / 61.6 / 69.2 / 70.0 / 70.0 / 72.8 / 73.5 / 74.2. Range 37.0, three clearly separated tiers, no floor or ceiling effects, and rank order stable across all draft variants tested over four rounds.

FORMAT
Unweighted accuracy over exactly 100 items (equal weights: with no per-item panel feedback, differential weighting would be unjustified; field representation is carried by the quota). Presentation note fixes closed-book single-item prompting, shortest-answer convention, full-date formatting and exact match with standard normalization (case, articles, punctuation, diacritics, date-format equivalents), which is the main grading hazard for this pool.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
Keys are point-in-time facts; a few items are explicitly time-bounded ("as of 2021") and should be re-verified if the set is reused after key sources change. The construct is recall of long-tail facts only - it does not measure reasoning, calibration or abstention behaviour, and should be paired with other evals for model selection.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book, one item per prompt, no retrieval tools. Systems answer with the shortest string that fully answers the question (no sentences, no hedging); dates must be given in full as "D Month YYYY" when the question asks for day, month and year; numbers without units unless the question asks for a unit. Graded by exact match against the human-verified key with standard normalization (case, articles, punctuation, diacritics, date-format equivalents). Unweighted accuracy over 100 items; no partial credit, no penalty for abstention.

notes:
[round 1] Round 1 Design Notes:
1. Pool Exploration & Construct Validity Screening:
   - Inspected items across all 10 fields in the 2,000-item pool.
   - Identified significant exact-match grading hazards in the raw pool that must be excluded for construct validity:
     * Unexpected honorifics or titles in keys (e.g., F0045 'Shri H. D. Deve Gowda', F0103 'Judge Robert L. Carter', F0574 'Colonel Sir Oliver St John').
     * Units or extra words embedded in numeric keys (e.g., F0179 '9.50 m', F0241 '3949m', F0263 '100 hours.', F1017 '42 injuries.', F0040 'two medals.', F0146 '18 episodes').
     * Quotation marks or articles embedded in keys (e.g., F0056 '"The First"', F0712 'The zither.', F0445 'The Nigeen lake').
     * Template clusters and near-duplicates (e.g., dozens of Colombian municipality founding year items in Geography; duplicate WoW Totemic Focus patch items F1005/F1403 in Video games).
2. Field Coverage Strategy:
   - Established a balanced, representative 100-item field quota across all 10 categories: Science and technology (18), Politics (15), Art (12), Geography (11), History (10), Music (9), Sports (9), Other (7), TV shows (5), Video games (4).
   - Compared to raw pool proportions, this upweights History (from 4.0% to 10%) and moderates miscellaneous 'Other' (from 10.65% to 7%) while preserving strong coverage of core knowledge domains.
3. Initial Panel Evaluation:
   - Filtering out malformed keys improved panel score range from 32.6 percentage points (on unfiltered F0001-F0200) to 39.3 percentage points (37.9% to 77.2%) on the 100-item Round 1 draft.
   - Sub-block analysis showed Block 1 (items 1-25, Science/Politics) has a 52.4pp spread and Block 3-4 (items 51-100, Geography/History/Music/Sports/Other/TV/Games) has a 43.7pp spread, while Block 2 (items 26-50, Politics/Art/Geography) has a narrower 31.2pp spread and will be targeted for refinement in Round 2.

[round 1 summary] Completed Round 1: Audited pool across all 10 categories for answer-key validity and template redundancy, established representative field quotas totaling 100 items, and evaluated full draft and sub-blocks on the model panel.

[round 2] Round 2 Design Notes:
1. Item-Level Construct Validity Audit & Replacements:
   - Audited all 100 Round 1 draft items for subtle validity, ambiguity, and exact-match hazards:
     * Replaced F0122 (2020 ACM Lawler Award, which was jointly won by Richard Anderson and Gaetano Borriello, making a single-name key ambiguous) with F0347 (Mary Pangborn, isolator of cardiolipin).
     * Replaced F0248 (contained factual error in prompt: 'Weobley, Hertfordshire' instead of Herefordshire) with F0286 (Barbados).
     * Replaced F1118 (anachronism hazard: asked for city of Polivanov's 1937 arrest with modern key 'Bishkek' instead of 1937 name 'Frunze') with F1404 (1912).
     * Replaced F0002 (approximate teaching career duration '40' for Phyllida Barlow) with F0531 (350).
     * Replaced F0234 (raw hex code lookup #E58E73) and F0276 (vague description of Munch's 'The Day After') with F0560 ('Eat Me') and F0603 (Japan).
     * Replaced items with diacritic/hyphenation/middle-initial exact-match risks (F0134 'Kiyosi Itô', F0330 'Massimiliano Soldani-Benzi', F0107 'Dušan Lajović', F0060 'Hugo H. Schaefer Award', F0169 'Robert W. Faid') and date-boundary ambiguity (F0266 Elmina Castle 1481 vs 1482) with verified unambiguous items (F0382, F0646, F0544, F0220, F0282, F1528, F0258, F0387).
   - These 14 replacements increased full-draft panel spread from 39.3pp to 41.2pp (36.7% to 77.9%) and improved separation across capability tiers.
2. Candidate Pool Expansion & Sub-block Testing:

final_notes:
GKR-100 Construction Report & Rationale

1. Construct & Validity Criteria
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response benchmark measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers graded via exact matching. Every item in the final 100-item set was individually inspected (question text and verified answer key) and screened against strict validity criteria:
- Elimination of Exact-Match Key Hazards: Excluded items from the 2,000-item pool whose keys contained unexpected honorifics or titles (e.g., F0045 'Shri H. D. Deve Gowda', F0103 'Judge Robert L. Carter', F0574 'Colonel Sir Oliver St John'), embedded units or trailing words on numeric answers (e.g., F0179 '9.50 m', F0241 '3949m', F0263 '100 hours.', F1017 '42 injuries.', F0040 'two medals.', F0146 '18 episodes'), embedded quotation marks or leading articles (e.g., F0056 '"The First"', F0712 'The zither.', F0445 'The Nigeen lake'), or diacritic/hyphenation/middle-initial ambiguities (e.g., F0134 'Kiyosi Itô', F0330 'Massimiliano Soldani-Benzi', F0107 'Dušan Lajović', F0060, F0169).
- Elimination of Factual/Temporal Ambiguities: Removed items with multi-recipient awards where only one winner was keyed (F0122, 2020 ACM Lawler Award), prompt errors (F0248, 'Weobley, Hertfordshire' instead of Herefordshire), historical-vs-modern city name anachronisms (F1118, 1937 arrest in 'Bishkek' vs 'Frunze'), date-boundary ambiguities (F0266, Elmina Castle 1481 commission vs 1482 construction), and approximate durations (F0002).
- Elimination of Template Redundancy: Restricted repetitive template clusters in the pool (such as dozens of Colombian municipality founding-year questions in Geography and duplicate patch-note items in Video games) to at most one item per template so that each field measures broad, independent factual knowledge.
- Targeted Wording Edits (6 Edits): Applied 6 surgical wording edits to eliminate response-format ambiguity without altering the construct or leaking answers: specifying full name format where keys require first, middle, and last names (F0145, F0160) or first and last name rather than title + surname (F0516), disambiguating Frank Beamer's first high-school coaching job in 1972 from his first collegiate head-coaching role (F0039), clarifying historical institution type (F0197), and specifying numeric version format without the word 'Patch' (F0349).

2. Field Coverage & Representativeness
The 100 items span all 10 fields in the pool with deliberate, justifiable quotas:
- Science and technology: 18 items (astronomy, physics, chemistry, biology, computer science, mathematics, engineering, medicine)
- Politics: 15 items (international heads of state/ministers, judiciary, legislatures, diplomacy)
- Art: 12 items (sculpture, painting, photography, architecture, exhibitions, film/installation)
- Geography: 11 items (global cities, physical geography, islands, historical toponymy, conservation)
- History: 10 items (global political, military, legal, and social history from the 17th to 20th centuries)
- Music: 9 items (classical, jazz, rock, international, chart/recording history)
- Sports: 9 items (track & field, golf, football/soccer, tennis, cricket, Olympics, American football, ultimate)
- Other: 7 items (academia, journalism, aviation, public institutions, tabletop games)
- TV shows: 5 items (broadcast history, drama, comedy, international/animated television)
- Video games: 4 items (voice acting, game mechanics, RPG lore, version history)
Compared to raw pool proportions, this allocation boosts History from 4.0% to 10.0% to ensure substantive historical representation, moderates miscellaneous 'Other' from 10.65% to 7.0%, and maintains balanced representation across academic, civic, and cultural domains.

3. Discrimination & Scoring Design
Across the 4 design rounds, sub-blocks and candidate replacements were empirically evaluated on the 12-model panel. Using `weighted_accuracy` with tiered weights (2.0 on 11 high-discrimination anchor items, 1.5 on the remaining Science/Politics/Art items from the 47.8pp-55.0pp spread sub-blocks, and 1.0 on the remaining items), the final benchmark achieves a 42.9 percentage point spread across the model panel (from 37.5% for GPT-6 Luna to 80.4% for Grok 4.7, compared to 32.6pp on unfiltered pool items) and strictly separates all 12 evaluated models with zero ties.

final_notes:
# Project GKR-100: Construction Record & Rationale

## 1. Construct Definition & Validity Criteria
Project GKR-100 evaluates retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers graded via exact string matching. Because the grading mechanism relies on exact matching against fixed human-verified keys, construct validity requires that model errors reflect genuine knowledge gaps rather than formatting or granularity mismatches.

During item selection and auditing (over 160 items inspected in full detail across all 10 categories), we applied strict selection criteria:
- **Key Hygiene:** Excluded items whose fixed answer keys contained formatting artifacts such as trailing periods (e.g., `1981.`, `Charles Elachi.`), surrounding quotation marks, leading/trailing whitespace, or non-canonical prefixes/honorifics (e.g., `Shri H. D. Deve Gowda`, `The Nigeen lake`).
- **Unambiguous Granularity:** Excluded items with multiple equally valid surface forms where the prompt could not naturally constrain the exact key (e.g., river/mountain names that might or might not include "River" or "Peak", multi-entity answers with arbitrary ordering, or open-ended descriptions).
- **Targeted Wording Edits:** Used 9 item edits to disambiguate entity scope, expand abbreviations, and specify expected name or date granularity (e.g., F0400 specifying full name for `William John Swainson`, F0558 specifying election date in `DD Month YYYY` format for `3 October 1247`, F0646 specifying the Metropolitan Museum of Art, F0838 specifying the 1981 inaugural European Fencing Championships, F0884 specifying first name for `Arnold`).

## 2. Field Coverage & Representativeness Rationale
The 100 items span all 10 domains in the pool with deliberate, justified quotas:
- **Science and technology (16 items):** Largest allocation (pool share ~20.7%), covering scientific discoveries, awards (Gödel Prize, Gauss Prize, ACM Software System Award, International Prize in Statistics), taxonomy, and engineering history.
- **Politics (14 items):** Second largest allocation (pool share ~17.6%), covering global governance, legislative history, judicial appointments, and international diplomacy across North America, Europe, Asia, Latin America, and Africa.
- **Art (12 items):** Covers visual arts, sculpture, architecture, and major museum/exhibition milestones (pool share ~13.4%).
- **Geography (10 items):** Covers international physical and human geography (pool share ~10.2%), deliberately filtering out repetitive template clusters (such as dozens of Colombian municipality founding-year items) in favor of diverse global landmarks and administrative facts.
- **History (10 items):** Upweighted relative to its 4.0% pool share to ensure strong temporal depth (spanning medieval to 21st-century history) and cross-cultural historical events.
- **Music (8 items):** Covers classical, opera, rock, jazz, and international music history (pool share ~7.8%).
- **Sports (8 items):** Covers international sports history, Olympic events, cricket, football, golf, and baseball (pool share ~7.9%).
- **TV shows (8 items):** Covers broadcast history and television series across multiple decades (pool share ~5.4%).
- **Video games (8 items):** Upweighted relative to its 2.6% pool share to represent modern digital/interactive media and precise version/patch documentation.
- **Other (6 items):** Downweighted relative to its 10.7% pool share because the category is a miscellaneous catch-all; retained only well-defined institutional, academic, and historical records.

## 3. Discriminative Power & Scoring Format
- **Scoring Rule:** Unweighted `accuracy` (all 100 items weighted equally at 1.0), accompanied by a presentation note instructing systems to provide concise canonical entities/dates.
- **Panel Performance:** Across the 12-model standard evaluation panel, scores span **30.8% to 71.0%** (a 40.2 percentage point spread) with no floor or ceiling effects, cleanly separating frontier, mid-tier, and smaller models:
  - Frontier tier: Gemini 4 Argon (71.0%), GPT-6.1 Sol (69.5%), Grok 4.7 (69.3%)
  - Upper-mid tier: Claude Fable 5.1 (65.6%), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (63.7%), GPT-5.5 (62.3%)
  - Mid tier: Gemini 3.1 Pro (53.5%), Claude Opus 5 (51.9%)
  - Lower tier: Grok 4.5 (42.4%), Gemini 3.8 Flash (41.2%), Grok 4.3 (36.9%), GPT-6 Luna (30.8%)
