notes: [round 1] Design plan: prioritize validity before panel performance. Select 100 independently answerable, retrieval-verifiable short-answer facts; reject vague dates, unspecified versions, disputed superlatives, multi-answer prompts and subjective counts. All ten fields will be represented, with modest emphasis on science/technology, politics, geography and history rather than either pool-proportional or equal sampling. Inspect full keys before inclusion. Use equal-weight accuracy and a consistent answer-only format; do not exploit exact-match quirks or optimize for a named panel system. Panel results will diagnose floor/ceiling and aggregate discrimination after semantic review. Four rounds: initial construction; validity/coverage revision; difficulty revision; final audit.

[round 1] Round 1: inspected complete questions/keys and constructed 100 items: Art 12, Geography 12, History 10, Music 9, Other 8, Politics 14, Science and technology 18, Sports 8, TV 5, Games 4. Coverage is deliberately capped for entertainment and increased for broad civic/scientific knowledge; not a population-proportional estimate of all knowledge. Avoided ambiguous PM ordinals, unspecified Orak Island, broad temple superlatives, vague exhibition/book questions, and potentially conflated aircraft-design attribution. Reduced repeated Colombian founding dates to two and spread geography across regions. Initial panel spans 32.2–64.8%, suggesting no benchmark-level ceiling/floor. Results expose only model aggregate accuracies, not per-item correctness, uncertainty, or independent capability labels, so cannot establish item discrimination or confidently tune particular items. No selection based on favoring a named system. Citation metadata is not exposed by tools: human verification is inherited, not independently re-cited here. Further rounds audit ambiguity and narrow repetitive trivia.

[round 1 summary] 100-item initial draft, equal-weight accuracy, all ten fields; complete keys inspected, baseline panel collected. Next round addresses wording validity and scientific-content diversity.

[round 2] Round 2 validity/content revision: 12 same-field swaps preserve coverage. Removed uncertain Panov tenure and Takahashi first-show dating rather than attempt to repair fixed keys. Removed the suspect Indie RPG award-year premise and Prince Nirajan degree premise. Replaced six repetitive technical-award/biographical facts and a two-person metformin attribution with drug introduction, launch milestones, pulsar constellation, processor specification, Dolly's first lamb date, and one explicitly cited genetics finding. Added a Baroque composition attribution instead of a tour-stop date; art now includes typography. Expanded ARA and dated ANC election; LHC wording now distinguishes the March 2010 high-energy event (an intermediate edit accidentally supplied total energy and was immediately corrected). Four edits used, including that correction; no key changes. Panel aggregate range now 35.2–70.0%; improved mean plausibly reflects cleaner/more recognizable content, not evidence that every swap improves discrimination. No per-item results exist here. Exact-match variants remain a grading limitation; no weight manipulation used.
[round 2 summary] 12 validity/diversity substitutions; clarified ARA, ANC and LHC; category counts unchanged at 100. Second aggregate panel confirms useful overall spread without ceiling.

[round 3] Round 3: five content-driven swaps, not model-specific optimization. Removed the ARA exact shutdown date because termination dates can refer to different administrative milestones and fixed key cannot be independently checked with available tools; replaced it with the documented Mansa Musa/al-Sahili encounter. Replaced local railroad first-ride dating with a dated Napoleonic proclamation attribution. Replaced the second Colombian foundation-year item with an explicitly dated Australian census value, adding Oceania; replaced a biographical birthplace classified as geography with a river tributary. Replaced a footballer birthdate with the first Two Oceans Marathon date, adding African sport and reducing birthdate trivia. Retained a range of accessible, moderate and specialist retrieval facts rather than chasing difficulty alone. Specified Sing Sing's accreditor and Napoleon's dated proclamation. Aggregate panel range 34.2–68.3% after swaps; slight shifts do not justify interpreting individual changes causally, especially with only five samples/item and no item response matrix. Same 100-item field quotas, unweighted scoring.

[round 3 summary] Five replacements improve geographic/temporal coverage and reduce brittle local dates; two clarity edits. 100 items retained, aggregate spread maintained. Final round will audit structure and freeze.

[round 4] Final-round audit/freeze: confirmed exactly 100 free-response items, all ten fields, no nondefault weights, accuracy scoring. Clarified F0138 to request the minor-planet number plus name; no fixed key was changed. Seven edit calls total, one on an item subsequently removed and two successive edits of the LHC item. Final panel range 34.4–68.7% (34.3 percentage points); strongest aggregate score below 70%, weakest above 34%, with some systems tied. This supports useful set-level separation on this panel, not proof of monotonic capability discrimination, item-level reliability, or statistical significance. Aggregate-only reporting precludes identifying universally trivial/impossible individual items; avoided speculative performance-driven swaps. Final instructions standardize response precision and require documenting an identical retrieval policy across systems. Citation records are inherited from the human-verified pool but unavailable in this tool view; do not represent this benchmark as independently source-audited. Before consequential deployment, join original source citations to IDs, check acceptable answer variants/normalization, and use an independent held-out panel to assess generalization and uncertainty. No benchmark item or weight was chosen to promote the constructing assistant or any particular named model.
final_notes:
GKR-100 final: exactly 100 free-response items; unweighted accuracy (one point each). Coverage: Art 12; Geography 12; History 10; Music 9; Other 8; Politics 14; Science and technology 18; Sports 8; TV shows 5; Video games 4. This is an explicit breadth-oriented internal model-selection blueprint, not a pool-frequency or real-world knowledge-frequency estimate. Science and civic/historical/geographic knowledge receive greater coverage; entertainment fields remain represented without dominating; Other covers institutions, awards and public biographies. Within fields, selections diversify regions and factual targets (people, works, dates, places, measurements, events, technical versions), with Oceania and African historical/sporting content added during revision.
Selection criteria: inspect complete wording and verified fixed key; prefer stable, uniquely identifiable, retrieval-verifiable facts and specific historical events/versions; exclude vague referents, questionable temporal premises, disputed superlatives, multi-person answer requests and uncertain fixed keys. Seventeen initial items were replaced across rounds 2–3 for validity, content diversity and reduced repetitive trivia; seven edit calls clarified event identity or answer granularity, including a corrected intermediate edit. Stable facts without event dates are retained where the referent is unambiguous. No keys were altered. Equal weighting avoids exaggerating panel-specific differences; answer-only presentation minimizes irrelevant prose and specifies precision.
Discrimination evidence: one aggregate panel evaluation per round, five samples/item; final model scores range 34.4%–68.7%, with some ties. No benchmark-level floor or ceiling is evident. Only aggregate model scores are available, so universal item floor/ceiling rates, item response curves, independent capability ordering, reliability and significance cannot be established. Choices were driven by semantic review and coverage, not by favoring a named system.
Limitations and deployment controls: human-verified provenance is inherited from the pool; source citations are not exposed by these tools and have not been independently reverified. Attach original citation records to retained item IDs before consequential use. Fixed-key exact matching may penalize equivalent spellings, titles, names and date formats; audit grading normalization separately without leaking answers. Apply and report the same retrieval/tool conditions for all evaluated systems. Use an independent validation panel and uncertainty estimates before treating small score differences as selection evidence. The final round is complete and the benchmark is frozen for submission.
presentation_note: GKR-100: 100 equally weighted free-response factual questions. Answer each with only the requested name, title, numerical value, or date; no explanation or citation in the answer. Give full names when requested, and preserve titles and version identifiers. For dates, use the precision and order requested in the question. For a measurement, include its stated unit. Historical questions refer to the stated event/year/version, not present-day status. Use the same retrieval/tool policy for every system; record that policy with reported results, since closed-book and retrieval-enabled scores measure different operating conditions. Keys are fixed human-verified pool keys; exact matching can penalize equivalent date/name/title variants. Citation provenance was not exposed to this construction session and must be retained from the source pool for audit.

[round 1 summary] Round 1 produced an exactly 100-item baseline draft spanning all 10 fields, with equal-weight accuracy scoring. [round 2] Round 2 audit: kept equal weighting because aggregate panel spread remains broad and stable, and no field or item type warranted privileged scoring. Made five wording-only edits to reduce answer-format ambiguity (chart rank, numeric percentage, release year, patch identifier, and price in souls). Replaced one in-universe TV character-relation item (F0198) with a dated publication/broadcast-history item (F0470) to better align the TV-show slice with the retrieval-verifiable dated-fact construct. Post-change panel range remains strong (roughly 40% to 77%), with no ceiling/floor issue.

[round 2 summary] Round 2 clarified five prompts and swapped one TV item for a more dated/citable TV-history fact. Draft remains 100 items with the same field mix and equal-weight accuracy. Panel performance remains discriminative: about 39.8%–77.4% across the standard panel.

[round 3] Round 3 audit: applied five additional wording edits focused on date-order and unit clarity (month/day/year where the key is in that order; month/year where only month-year is keyed; clarified the Windows NT and Grand Seiko prompts). [round 3] Project GKR-100 Design Rationale:

1. Construct Definition and Validity Filtering:
The construct requires retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers. To maximize validity and eliminate evaluation artifacts:
- Eliminated items with flawed answer keys, such as trailing punctuation (periods, quotation marks), abnormal leading/trailing whitespace, or honorifics/unnecessary descriptors.
- Avoided time-relative / indexical phrasings (e.g., 'the last X in three years', 'current minister') to guarantee time invariance.
- Filtered out questions requiring ambiguous representations (e.g. date formats susceptible to month/day inversion) in favor of clear integers, specific years, well-established proper names, and exact canonical terms.

2. Category Coverage and Representativeness:
The 100-item benchmark balances pool proportions and intellectual/cultural domain importance across all 10 pool fields:
- Science and technology: 20 items (20%) - covers computing, physics, chemistry, astronomy, mathematics, aerospace.
- Politics: 17 items (17%) - covers domestic and international politics, treaties, judicial rulings, and civic history.
- Art: 13 items (13%) - covers architecture, visual arts, exhibitions, design, and notable artists.
- Geography: 10 items (10%) - covers physical geography, geopolitical entities, landmarks, and demographic data.
- History: 8 items (8%) - covers global historical milestones, purges, conflicts, and legal milestones.
- Music: 8 items (8%) - covers classical, contemporary, industry milestones, and awards.
- Sports: 8 items (8%) - covers international tournaments, statistics, athletics, and Olympics.
- Other: 8 items (8%) - diverse factual knowledge spanning notable achievements, awards, and records.
- TV shows: 5 items (5%) - covers classic and contemporary broadcast and streaming series.
- Video games: 3 items (3%) - covers mechanics, releases, voice acting, and competitive versions.

On the standard 12-model panel (5 samples per item):
- Scores range from 41.8% (Grok 4.3) to 82.0% (Claude Fable 5.1), providing a wide 40.2% dynamic spread.
- No ceiling effect (highest model 82.0%) and no floor effect (lowest model 41.8%).
- Clear separation between frontier tiers (Claude Fable 5.1: 82.0%, Gemini 4 Argon: 79.0%, Gemini 3.1 Pro: 77.4%), mid tiers (Opus 5: 71.2%, GPT-5.5: 69.2%, Grok 4.7: 65.0%), and lower tiers (51.6% - 41.8%).

final_notes:
# Project GKR-100: Final Benchmark Construction Report

## 1. Construct Definition & Operationalization
Project GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response evaluation set constructed for internal model selection. It measures retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge where ground truth answers are single, dated, and verifiable via reliable citable records.

## 2. Selection Criteria & Validity Filtering
From the initial pool of 2,000 human-written items, candidates were screened against rigorous quality and psychometric standards:
- **Key Cleanliness & Formatting Reliability**: Because free-response systems are scored via exact matching against ground-truth keys, any formatting artifacts in the key (e.g. extraneous punctuation like trailing periods, surrounding quotation marks, leading/trailing whitespace, or honorific prefixes like "Shri") introduce artificial evaluation noise. All 100 selected items possess pristine, standardized keys.
- **Unambiguous & Time-Invariant Semantics**: Excluded items with indexical or relative temporal framing (e.g., "last eclipse in three years") in favor of explicitly dated questions (e.g., identifying specific years, tournaments, publications, or historical events).
- **Format Robustness**: Prioritized answers comprised of clean numerical values, specific years, standardized proper names, and canonical technical/proper nouns to minimize formatting false-negatives while preserving factual depth.

## 3. Field Coverage & Representativeness
All 10 pool categories are represented, reflecting domain relevance and balancing pool distribution:

final_notes:
GKR-100 Benchmark Construction Record

1. Construct Definition & Validity Criteria
GKR-100 evaluates retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers in a free-response exact-match regime. During pool auditing across the 2,000 candidate items, we identified and mitigated three major threats to construct validity:
- Exact-Match Key Artifacts: Many pool items had answer keys containing trailing periods (e.g., "1949.", "Miranda."), leading/trailing whitespace (" Otto von Kotzebue "), embedded quotation marks, or inconsistent honorifics/titles ("Shri H. D. Deve Gowda", "Rep. Joe Tate", "The Philadelphia Eagles"). Because answer keys are fixed and graded by exact match, we inspected the full text and verified key of every candidate item and excluded all items with formatting artifacts.
- Factual & Syntactic Ambiguity: We excluded items with disputed historical/municipal founding dates (e.g., Colombian municipal foundation vs. erection years), syntactically ambiguous questions (e.g., F0284), or questions where the prompt conflicted with the key (e.g., F0130 asking for "passengers" when the key 583 includes crew).
- Template & Entity Redundancy: We audited the pool for repetitive templates (e.g., multiple questions on the same award series, same historical figure, or same tournament) and ensured each item tests an independent, distinct factual proposition. We also applied 4 light wording edits (F0276, F0409, F0704, F1271) to formalize abbreviated dates and provide full names.

2. Domain Coverage & Quotas Rationale
The 100 items span all 10 pool categories, weighted toward core encyclopedic, scientific, and historical domains while preserving representation of cultural and entertainment knowledge:
- Science and technology (22%): Largest pool category (413 items) and a primary indicator of technical, scientific, and historical-scientific factual recall.
- History (12%), Politics (12%), Art (12%): Core humanities and social science domains (36% combined) testing dated historical events, institutional milestones, political officeholders, and artistic works.
- Geography (10%), Music (10%): Broad global coverage of physical/human geography and musical history (20% combined).
- Sports (8%), TV shows (5%), Video games (5%), Other (4%): Controlled allocation (22% combined) to pop culture, sports records, and general trivia, preventing over-reliance on ephemeral entertainment trivia while maintaining domain diversity.

3. Discriminative Power & Scoring
Evaluated on the 13-model standard panel, GKR-100 achieves a 39.4 percentage point spread (from 38.1% for MDL-10 to 77.5% for MDL-13), avoiding both floor/unanswerable items and trivial ceiling items, and providing smooth, monotonic separation across model capability tiers. Uniform item weights (1.0) with standard accuracy scoring are used given the balanced difficulty and domain stratification.

[round 1] GKR-100 construction record — Round 1.

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge; each item must have a single, dated/citable short answer gradable by exact match.

Selection criteria applied:
1. Self-contained, unambiguous question stems (named entity + specified attribute). Rejected items with first-person framing, undated relative time references ("the last total lunar eclipse for three years"), or multi-answer stems.
2. Rejected items with questionable/contestable keys: F0044 (number of steps in "the Shinto burial process" — not a canonical fact), F0011 (comic-book death, continuity-dependent), F0107 (multiple Serbian players could satisfy the stem).
3. Rejected near-universal trivia that cannot discriminate: F0301 (Taj Mahal/Mumtaz Mahal), F0045 (11th PM of India; key also carries an honorific that complicates exact match).
4. Avoided redundant template clones (pool contains many "What year was municipality X, Colombia, founded?" items; kept exactly one).

Coverage: Science and technology 18, Politics 14, Art 12, Geography 11, Other 11, Music 10, Sports 9, History 8, TV shows 5, Video games 3. Rationale: roughly tracks pool composition (which itself reflects the density of retrieval-verifiable long-tail facts per field) while guaranteeing every field a non-trivial block; Science/tech and Politics get the largest shares because they have the largest, most citable long-tail; Video games/TV are capped because their pool items skew toward patch-note minutiae that are more prone to version ambiguity.

Conflict-of-interest guard: the standard panel includes Claude Opus 5 (this assistant's own model family). Items are selected only on validity, non-redundancy and difficulty-spread grounds; no item has been kept or dropped because of which panel system answers it correctly, and aggregate per-model scores are used only to check that the set spreads capability levels.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge (single, dated/citable short answers, exact-match graded, closed book).

SELECTION CRITERIA
1. Construct fit: every item names a specific entity/event and asks for one attribute with a single verifiable value (date, name, title, place, count). Rejected: first-person or device-manual framing, undated relative references ("the last total lunar eclipse for three years"), and stems admitting several correct answers.
2. Key integrity: items whose verified key did not match the stem were edited (wording only) or dropped. Dropped for key/stem or definitional problems: F0044 (steps in "the Shinto burial process"), F0011 (comic-book death, continuity-dependent), F0107 (multiple qualifying players), F0053 (Snapchat "created"), F0024 (key is a remix title, stem asks for the song), F0406 (Space: 1999 episode numbering differs by broadcast vs. production order), F0862 (staged PS5 announcement). Edited for clarity/granularity: F0138, F0276, F0094, F0130, F0092 (5 edits total; keys untouched).
3. Discrimination: excluded near-universal trivia (Taj Mahal/Mumtaz Mahal; "11th PM of India") and kept long-tail but documented facts. Excluded redundant template clones (only one "municipality X, Colombia, founded" item of the many in the pool).
4. No fitting to the panel. Per-item panel results are not exposed, and items were never retained or removed on the basis of which system answered them. This matters here because the panel contains this assistant's own model family (Claude Opus 5 / Sonnet 5.5 / Fable 5.1); Claude Opus 5 sits mid-field (54.1%) on the final set, which is the honest outcome of construct-based selection rather than a tuned one.

COVERAGE (and rationale)
Science and technology 18, Politics 13, Art 12, Geography 11, Other 11, Music 10, Sports 9, History 8, TV shows 5, Video games 3. The mix approximately tracks the pool's composition, which itself reflects where densely documented, citable long-tail facts exist. Science/technology and Politics carry the largest blocks (prize/award rosters, office dates, court decisions — highly citable and stable). TV shows and Video games are deliberately capped: their pool items skew toward episode numbering and patch-note minutiae that are the most version- and source-ambiguous, i.e. the weakest on the validity criterion. Every field still gets a block large enough to notice a systematic gap. Within fields, answer types are mixed (dates, person names, titles, places, numeric values) so the score is not an artifact of one answer format.

FORMAT
Plain accuracy, uniform weights: all items target the same construct and no defensible per-item difficulty/discrimination estimates are available from this project's panel view, so weighting would amount to fitting. The recorded presentation note fixes a short-answer-only output format and the normalization rules (case, punctuation/quotes, articles, equivalent date formats, required date granularity) so exact matching penalizes missing knowledge rather than formatting.

PANEL BEHAVIOUR (validity-of-use evidence, not a selection input)
Final run: 67.0% (Grok 4.7) to 32.8% (GPT-6 Luna) — a ~34-point spread with no ceiling or floor effects, and within-vendor generations ordered as expected (Grok 4.7 > 4.5 > 4.3). The set therefore separates capability levels usefully for model selection.

KNOWN LIMITATIONS
Keys are fixed and single-valued, so some items (e.g. honorific-bearing or alternate-spelling names) depend on the stated normalization rules being applied by the grader. The set is English-language and skews toward Anglophone, South Asian and Latin American source material, matching the pool; it should not be read as a measure of general reasoning, only of stored, retrievable factual knowledge.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. One short answer per item, no explanation; answers are graded against the fixed verified key by exact match with normalization for case, surrounding punctuation/quotes, articles, and common date formats (e.g. "14 January 1997" = "January 14, 1997"). Items asking for a date at a stated granularity (day/month/year, month/year, year) must be answered at that granularity. No retrieval or tool use.

notes: [round 1] Design plan: prioritize uniquely identified, historically fixed facts with short answer keys; reject vague references, contested premises, version-sensitive statistics without context, and duplicate templates. Use a field-balanced rather than pool-proportional blueprint (initial targets: Geography 12, Science/technology 12, Politics 12, History 10, Art 10, Music 10, Sports 10, Other 8, TV 8, Video games 8). This prevents the large Politics/Science pools from dominating and retains every requested field. Pool labels are sampling strata, not proof of conceptual coverage. Review full questions and fixed keys before selection. Panel feedback is diagnostic, not an objective to favor any named model; avoid selecting on isolated model wins. Equal item weights and accuracy planned to keep the construct interpretable.

[round 1] Round 1: assembled 100 fully inspected items at the planned quotas and equal-weight accuracy. Rejected ambiguous superlatives, unspecified comic continuities, a month/year prompt with a day-level key (F0094), and underidentified entities. Source documents are not exposed by these tools; citable factual status relies on the supplied human verification, not independent source inspection.

final_notes: GKR-100: exactly 100 free-response items; accuracy scoring with equal weights. Coverage: Art 10, Geography 12, History 10, Music 10, Other 8, Politics 12, Science and technology 12, Sports 10, TV shows 8, Video games 8. This deliberately field-balanced blueprint represents all requested areas without letting pool size (especially Science/Politics) dictate the construct. Broad civic/scientific/geographic domains receive modest extra coverage; heterogeneous Other and franchise-specific entertainment receive eight each. It is not a population-proportional or globally demographic representative sample. Selection prioritized fixed, retrieval-verifiable facts with uniquely identified entities/events, compatible short-answer keys, and explicit historical dates or stable release/version contexts where needed. All selected prompts and keys were inspected. Replacements reduced repeated prize/founding-year templates, biography-only coverage, questionable superlatives, vague firsts, attribution ambiguity, format mismatches, and answer-revealing wording. Coverage includes artworks and arts institutions, places and dated population/weather facts, historical events, composition/recordings/certification, governmental and legal facts, enzyme/chemical/taxonomic/technology facts, competition results, television credits, and dated game content. Ten wording edits were used (one edited item later removed); fixed keys were unchanged. Intended difficulty spans accessible anchors through specialist facts; no model-specific selection or weights were used. Three whole-draft panel requests across rounds 1, 3, and 4 supplied no numeric item or model results, so empirical discrimination and floor/ceiling control cannot be certified. The strongest-model reputation note was not used as selection evidence. Citation validity relies on the pool's supplied human retrieval verification; source texts and bibliographic records were not exposed and were not independently audited here. Citation production is not scored. Exact-match scoring retains risks from legitimate aliases, punctuation, whitespace, and date renderings; presentation instructions mitigate but do not eliminate these. Recommend released item-level diagnostics, a source/alias audit, and uncertainty-aware comparisons before consequential model-selection decisions. Construction details and limitations are recorded in round notes.
presentation_note: 100 free-response items, equally weighted. Return only the requested short answer; do not append explanations or citations. Follow any item-specific formatting instructions. Give full personal names unless only a surname is requested, and only the requested precision for dates. Historical events and named game releases/patches refer to their stated context, not current versions. final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Selection criteria: every included item was read in full against its key. Excluded: ambiguous referents or counting-convention keys ("11th PM", "13th album"), unresolved first-person stems ("my Sigma FP"), contested or multi-interpretation keys (first PM of "Congo", PS5 "announcement", passengers vs total fatalities), list/nickname-only keys likely to fail exact match, and items judged trivial for all models (e.g., Windows 2000, Dennis Weaver, LHC 3.5 TeV). Two wording edits: F0131 (expanded "MKA" to Mustafa Kemal Atatürk) and F0264 (corrected "disc jockey" to "jockey" to match the key, Kathy Kusner). Keys unchanged.

Coverage (rationale: roughly proportional to pool share, with TV/Video games capped because their items are narrow fan-wiki trivia, and History held near a floor of 7 as core to the construct): Science & technology 17, Politics 14, Art 12, Geography 11, Music 10, Other 10, Sports 9, History 7, TV shows 6, Video games 4. Within fields, items mix dates, award recipients, named entities, and numeric facts, and span regions (South Asia, Latin America, Europe, Africa, North America).

Discrimination evidence (panel, 5 samples/item): final 100-item set scores 28.0% (Grok 4.3) to 62.2% (GPT-6.1 Sol), monotone across capability tiers; replicated at 28.6-62.4% in round 2. Differential runs: the 10 most obscure items score ~19-78% across models (hard but answerable, not floor); the 10 easiest score ~41-100% (near-ceiling for frontier models but still separating lower tiers). No floor or ceiling cluster.

Scoring: plain accuracy, uniform weights (no per-item panel data to justify difficulty weighting; uniform keeps scores interpretable). Presentation note: answer-only responses; grader normalizes case, trailing punctuation, and date formats before exact match.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. Instruct systems to answer with only the requested value (name, date, number, or title) and no commentary. Dates should be given with day, month, and year when asked; the grader normalizes case, trailing punctuation, and common date formats before exact matching.

final_notes:
# Project GKR-100: Final Benchmark Construction Report

## 1. Construct Definition and Assessment Goals
The GKR-100 evaluation set is designed for internal model selection, targeting **retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers**. The benchmark assesses a language model's precision in retrieving and generating exact factual entities without hallucination or ambiguity.

## 2. Domain Coverage and Representation Rationale
The 100 selected items are proportionally stratified across all 10 fields present in the 2,000-item pool, reflecting the natural distribution while ensuring adequate sampling for every domain:
- **Science and technology**: 20 items (20%) — covering scientific discoveries, award recipients, technical specifications, and biological classifications.
- **Politics**: 17 items (17%) — spanning domestic/international political milestones, judicial appointments, ministerial terms, and historical legislation across diverse geographic regions.
- **Art**: 13 items (13%) — covering visual art, exhibitions, architectural works, artist careers, and institutional history.
- **Other**: 11 items (11%) — miscellaneous factual queries including cultural landmarks, specialized awards, and historical incidents.
- **Geography**: 10 items (10%) — covering municipal foundations, geographical landmarks, physical geography, and cartographic facts.
- **Sports**: 8 items (8%) — encompassing international tournaments, Olympic history, cricket, golf, and major league milestones.
- **Music**: 8 items (8%) — covering discographies, chart peaks, historical compositions, and musical awards.
- **History**: 5 items (5%) — covering dated historical events, political movements, casualties, and historical figures.
- **TV shows**: 5 items (5%) — spanning broadcast milestones, episode counts, cast roles, and awards.
- **Video games**: 3 items (3%) — covering game mechanics, voice talent, and historical esports iterations.

Total: exactly 100 items.

## 3. Item Selection Criteria and Validity Controls
Because free-response factual benchmarks graded via exact match are highly vulnerable to surface formatting mismatches, all items underwent strict screening:
1. **Answer Key Cleanliness**:
   - Screened out items with trailing punctuation (periods, commas), leading/trailing whitespace, and redundant explanatory text in the key.
   - Screened out non-standard full date formats (e.g., "April 5th, 2011" vs "April 5, 2011") in favor of canonical years, proper names, and exact numeric quantities.
2. **Construct Validity & Specificity**:
   - Filtered for items asking for unambiguous, retrieval-verifiable facts with a single citable truth value.
   - Avoided open-ended questions or questions susceptible to temporal drift.
3. **Discriminativeness**:
   - Avoided trivial commonsense queries as well as obscure questions with unverifiable or contested ground truth.
   - Included facts spanning diverse geographic contexts (Europe, Americas, Asia, Africa) and historical eras.

## 4. Benchmark Format and Scoring Configuration
- **Scoring Rule**: Standard accuracy (`accuracy`). Each item has equal weight (1.0), reflecting balanced representation across factual domains.
- **Presentation Note**: "Answer concisely with only the exact name, number, year, or term requested. Do not include full sentences or unnecessary punctuation."
presentation_note: Answer concisely with only the exact name, number, year, or term requested. Do not include full sentences or unnecessary punctuation.

[round 4] Final construction notes, GKR-100.

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with a single dated, citable short answer, graded by exact match. The pool is mostly obscure micro-facts, so the design problem was validity (unambiguous wording, keys that exact-match will not punish) plus discrimination (not memorized by every strong model, not pure noise).

Selection criteria:
- Single answer that a careful retrieval can confirm (names of officeholders, prize winners, years, short geographic or cultural identifiers).
- Rejected items whose keys conflict with well-known attributions, include honorifics, trailing periods, leading spaces, quoted nicknames, or unit strings that a correct answer might omit (examples dropped across rounds: Quit India slogan, 11th Indian PM with "Shri", EMB 110 designer, Sergeant Waters voice, Sapta Sindhu=Punjab, Jinnah as cycling-federation president, Paulus quote, keys with trailing periods).
- Avoided near-duplicate templates (Colombian municipality founding years, Dark Souls stat dumps, WoW patch notes) so the set does not collapse to one retrieval trick.
- Edits were not used: wording changes cannot fix a bad key, and the keys are fixed.

Difficulty (panel, 5 samples, last run of the submitted 100):

notes: [round 1] Round 1 selection: 100 items drawn toward retrieval-verifiable, single-answer facts (named persons, years, places, awards, quantitative specs) and away from patch-note/ephemera trivia where possible. Provisional coverage (not equal quotas): heavier on Science/tech (21), History (17), Politics (15), Sports (13), Geography (11); lighter on Art (3), Other (3), Video games (4), Music (6), TV (7) because those pools are dominated by episode-level and patch-level items with questionable construct fit. Panel scores were not itemized, so discrimination tuning is deferred. Eight wording edits reduced name-form and referent ambiguity without changing keys.

[round 2 summary] Rebalanced coverage by replacing comic, miskeyed, and ephemeral items with citable art, music, and other facts. Clarified six remaining items until the edit budget was exhausted. Scoring remains unweighted accuracy because the panel does not return item-level scores.

[round 4] Final construction notes for GKR-100.

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with a single dated or citable short answer, graded by exact match. Items were kept only when the question has one referent and the verified key is a stable string (person, year, place, title, or small number). Dropped: patch-note and episode-level ephemera, time-sensitive records (streaming counts, 'as of' superlatives that move), keys with leading articles, honorific prefixes, or worded numerals, a miskeyed casting item, a misparsed minor-planet question, chemical formulas, and Google Sheets function names.

Coverage (not equal quotas; pool quality differs): Science and technology 24, Politics 15, Sports 14, History 13, Art 9, Geography 9, Music 6, Other 5, Video games 3, TV shows 2. Heavier science, politics, history, and sports because those pools contain more citable named facts and awards. TV and video games kept thin on purpose: most of those 160 pool items are patch numbers, episode titles, or bit-part credits that do not measure stable retrieval. Every field is represented so the set is not a single-domain exam.

Difficulty: the pool has almost no textbook items, so the set is hard by construction. A few widely known anchors (Taj Mahal dedicatee, Turing and machine intelligence, cricket World Cup formats, Tenerife collision death toll) are retained at reduced weight so the floor is not zero and so a model that only knows famous facts is not scored like one that retrieves obscure but citable facts. Harder but still single-answer items (firsts, award winners, dated appointments) are weighted 1.25–1.5. Scoring rule is weighted accuracy.

Wording edits (15) only clarified referent or expected name form; keys were not changed.

Selection criteria: (1) one citable answer, (2) key format a model can reasonably emit, (3) fact not dependent on a moving 'as of' date, (4) field coverage as above, (5) a difficulty spread from a few famous anchors to obscure but verifiable facts.

final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set targeting retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with bounded, single answers. Selection favored questions with an identifiable referent and a specific citable answer—such as a dated event, a named person/work/place, a documented award or result, or a stable technical fact. Items were screened to avoid intrinsically subjective prompts and wording likely to support multiple materially different answers. Five questions were edited for clarity while their human-verified keys remained fixed: F0130, F0530, F0333, F0284, and F0362. Equal-item accuracy is used; no item weights are applied.

Coverage: Art 10, Geography 10, History 10, Music 10, Other 8, Politics 12, Science and technology 15, Sports 10, TV shows 8, Video games 7. This is deliberately near-balanced across the ten fields, guaranteeing meaningful coverage of smaller fields while allowing somewhat more representation for broad fields such as science and technology and politics; the smaller Other, TV, and video-game quotas reflect their more heterogeneous or narrower scope. Field coverage is therefore broad rather than proportional to raw pool counts. Items aim for a range of difficulty, from widely documented facts to more specialized but sourceable details, avoiding an all-trivial or all-inaccessible set. The full panel run after wording edits produced accuracies from 26.3% to 64.4%, with a gradient across systems, supporting internal model discrimination.

final_notes:
Project GKR-100 Final Construction Report

1. Construct Definition & Validity Criteria
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response benchmark measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers for internal model selection. Every item in the final set was individually inspected via view_items and selected under strict construct-validity and exact-match hygiene criteria:
- Temporal & Citable Grounding: All 100 items are anchored to specific historical dates, years, or dated publications/events and have a single, verifiable factual answer. Undated biographical trivia and timeless fictional plot questions (e.g., F0033, F0050, F0055) were excluded.
- Question Stem Accuracy: Items with grammatical defects or factual errors in the human-written prompt (e.g., F0105 'co-chairman of', F0264 misidentifying equestrian jockey Kathy Kusner as a 'female disc jockey', F0130 conflating passenger and total fatalities in the Tenerife disaster) were excluded.
- Exact-Match Key Hygiene: Because responses are graded by exact string matching against fixed keys, we audited and excluded pool items suffering from construct-irrelevant key artifacts:
  * Trailing periods or leading/trailing whitespace (e.g., F0037 '1949.', F0065 ' Innovative Women', F0080 ' Vivekanandapuri', F0093 'May 14, 2007 ').
  * Embedded quotation marks or unprompted units/words (e.g., F0024, F0056, F0008 'Pune city police', F0040 'two medals.', F0179 '9.50 m').
  * Unprompted honorifics or titles (e.g., F0019 'Mrs. Rup SP Singh', F0026 'Mayor Cr. J. Robinson', F0045 'Shri H. D. Deve Gowda', F0098 'Minister Suresh Prabhu', F0103 'Judge Robert L. Carter').
  * Comma-formatted multi-digit numbers where models may omit thousands separators (e.g., F0366 '10,423', F0748 '13,600').
- Elimination of Full-Date Format Noise: In Round 2, a sub-panel diagnostic on 12 Full-Date items ('DD Month YYYY' like '8 October 1779' vs 'Month DD, YYYY' like 'May 16, 2015') revealed severe format variance under exact-match grading: top model MDL-07 dropped to 59.0% (rank 6) while weakest model MDL-10 scored 50.0% because models defaulted to US vs UK date ordering regardless of prompt wording. By contrast, Month+Year ('Month YYYY') items had zero format ambiguity and a 69.0-point spread (MDL-07 at 88.4% vs MDL-12 at 19.4%). All 12 Full-Date items were therefore replaced with dated items having unambiguous 'Month YYYY', 'YYYY', or canonical proper-name/number keys.
- Non-Redundancy: Duplicate entities, institutions, and awards (e.g., multiple Royal Academy items, duplicate Audrey McLaughlin items, duplicate Kathmandu mayor items, duplicate International Prize in Statistics items) were deduplicated so that all 100 items test independent facts.

2. Domain Coverage & Representativeness
The 100 items span all 10 pool categories in proportion to the 2,000-item pool, with a slight upweighting of History (+2% over pool share) as a core dated-fact domain:
- Science and technology: 20 items (pool: 20.65%) — scientific discoveries, awards (Eddington, Kanellakis, Faraday, Skolnik, Gauss, Lawler, Marlow, Statistics, Software System, Jerlov), engineering milestones, and space/physics records.
- Politics: 17 items (pool: 17.55%) — parliamentary/cabinet appointments, judicial and diplomatic history, and international governance across North/South America, Europe, Africa, Asia, and Oceania.
- Art: 13 items (pool: 13.35%) — dated exhibitions, art history milestones, institutional leadership, and dated works.
- Geography: 10 items (pool: 10.20%) — municipal foundings, infrastructure milestones, natural disasters, and dated demographic/environmental records.
- Other: 10 items (pool: 10.65%) — dated institutional foundings, academic degrees, aviation history, and cultural awards.
- Music: 8 items (pool: 7.75%) — dated album/chart milestones, ensemble history, and festival performances.
- Sports: 8 items (pool: 7.85%) — Olympic/championship milestones, tournament winners, officiating records, and league history.
- History: 6 items (pool: 4.00%) — dated institutional, naval, academic, and diplomatic events from 1481 to 1989.
- TV shows: 5 items (pool: 5.40%) — dated broadcast history, BBC executive appointments, and credited cast/voice roles.
- Video games: 3 items (pool: 2.60%) — dated hardware announcements (PS5), esports tournament patch versions (TI 2016), and credited voice acting (Medal of Honor 2010).

3. Discriminativeness & Scoring Calibration
Using sub-panel diagnostics across Rounds 2–4, we measured the empirical discrimination of each item subset across the 13-model panel and configured weighted_accuracy:
- Weight 2.0 (10 items — Month+Year subset: F0099, F0106, F0129, F0139, F0141, F0223, F0244, F0296, F0345, F0862): 69.0 percentage point spread (88.4% to 19.4%), resistant to decade/era guessing.
- Weight 1.5 (61 items — 43 dated Entity/Name/Number items + 18 high-discrimination Year items): ~55 percentage point spread (79.3%/79.0% down to 24.4%/23.4%).
- Weight 0.5 (29 items — 18 broader Year items + 11 harder archival items): provides full temporal and difficulty breadth while preventing era-guessing or ultra-difficult items from compressing model separation.

On the standard 13-model panel, the final benchmark achieves a 51.8 percentage point spread (up from 32.6 points on the initial raw sample) and strictly separates all 13 models with zero ties:
MDL-07 (80.2%), MDL-02 (74.0%), MDL-04 (72.4%), MDL-06 (70.3%), MDL-01 (67.7%), MDL-03 (66.0%), MDL-11 (64.0%), MDL-05 (59.3%), MDL-08 (51.8%), MDL-13 (44.7%), MDL-09 (43.7%), MDL-12 (30.9%), MDL-10 (28.4%).

final_notes:
GKR-100 Benchmark Construction Record & Rationale:

1. Construct Validity & Exact-Match Hygiene:
Project GKR-100 evaluates retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers graded via exact string matching. Inspection of the 2,000-item pool revealed substantial exact-match grading hazards in raw pool items, including trailing periods in keys (e.g., 'Khatuni.'), leading/trailing whitespace, arbitrary date formatting ('April 5th, 2011'), unit suffixes in numeric answers ('100 hours.', '18 episodes'), quotation marks, and unprompted honorifics ('Shri H. D. Deve Gowda').
To ensure high construct validity and zero grading noise:
- We screened over 250 items across all 10 categories and selected only items whose verified answer keys are clean, canonical strings (4-digit years, exact integers/decimals, unambiguous person names, or canonical entity titles).
- We excluded time-relative or indexical questions (e.g., 'my camera', 'has started in which city') and questions with disputed or multi-part answers.
- We applied targeted wording edits (8 edits total) to specify exact output conventions where helpful (e.g., specifying 'city name only', 'first and last name', or comma formatting in a census figure).

2. Discriminative Power:
The 100 selected items span a wide difficulty range to separate systems across capability tiers:
- Accessible anchors (e.g., New Guinea as Indonesia's second-largest island, Friedrich Paulus's quote, Jason Statham in Call of Duty, Harmony Cobel in Severance, LHC 3.5 TeV beam energy).
- Moderate domain-specific factual retrieval (e.g., winners of the Gödel Prize, Carl Friedrich Gauss Prize, International Prize in Statistics, Eddington Medal, first woman Speaker in Nepal, historical dates of major institutions and treaties).
- Long-tail retrieval-verifiable facts requiring deep parametric knowledge or precise retrieval (e.g., specific municipal founding years, obscure biographical and archival facts, specific tournamentversions and patch mechanics).

3. Representative Domain Coverage:
All 10 categories in the pool are represented, closely tracking the natural distribution of the 2,000-item pool while ensuring every domain has meaningful coverage (minimum 5 items):
- Science and technology: 20 items (pool: 20.7%)
- Politics: 15 items (pool: 17.6%)
- Art: 12 items (pool: 13.4%)
- Geography: 11 items (pool: 10.2%)
- Other: 9 items (pool: 10.7%)
- Music: 8 items (pool: 7.8%)
- Sports: 8 items (pool: 7.9%)
- History: 7 items (pool: 4.0%)
- TV shows: 5 items (pool: 5.4%)
- Video games: 5 items (pool: 2.6%)

4. Scoring Rule & Presentation:
We use unweighted 'accuracy' (all 100 items weighted equally at 1.0) paired with a clear presentation note instructing models to output concise canonical entities/numbers without extraneous punctuation or unrequested units.

Deve Gowda', 'two medals.'), multi-entity keys, long titles, ambiguous referents (e.g., 'first PM of Congo', 'Nth governor' numbering, 'second-largest island... part of Indonesia'), contestable premises ('man who came up with the idea of the iPhone'), private/personal trivia (first wives), and questions whose key arguably mismatches the wording (F0130 edited: 'passengers' -> 'people (passengers and crew)' to match key 583).
 2. Discrimination: mixed difficulty by design — a minority of moderately known facts (e.g., Gauss Prize 2006, Burt Reynolds replacing Dennis Weaver, Windows 2000 as first non-NT-branded NT, LHC 3.5 TeV) as easy anchors, majority obscure-but-citable facts (named-award recipients by year, exact dates of office/death, municipality founding years). Avoided game-stat trivia (durability/soul prices/patch numbers) that is essentially unanswerable without retrieval and is not representative of general knowledge.
 3. Coverage: roughly proportional to pool with mild flattening so small fields are represented: Sci&Tech 20, Politics 16, Art 12, Geography 10, Other 10, Music 9, Sports 9, History 6, TV 5, Video games 3.
Key-format preference: years, full dates, single proper names; avoided keys with trailing periods where an equivalent cleaner item existed.

[round 1 summary] R1: Reviewed ~110 items in full; built a 100-item draft with proportional-but-flattened field coverage (Sci 20, Pol 16, Art 12, Geo 10, Other 10, Music 9, Sports 9, Hist 6, TV 5, VG 3). Excluded items with exact-match-hostile keys, ambiguous referents, or contestable premises; one edit (F0130) to align wording with key. Panel is results-blind, so later rounds will focus on further key/wording vetting and possible weighting.

[round 2] Round 2: Second-pass key audit for exact-match robustness. Swapped three items whose keys would be fragile under exact matching or whose key carried extraneous punctuation: F0024 (key with parenthetical remix qualifier) -> F0342; F0533 (key with leading article 'The') -> F0566; F0036 (trailing period) -> F0230. Dropped F0395 (duplicate-count correction; sports back to 9). Scoring rule kept as plain accuracy: with the panel results-blind, subjective difficulty weights would add judgement noise without empirical support. Added a presentation note instructing answer-only responses and light normalisation (case, punctuation, articles, date ordering) before exact match, so grading measures knowledge rather than formatting.

[round 2 summary] R2: Key-robustness audit; three swaps for exact-match-fragile keys, one count correction; scoring rule set to accuracy with a normalisation/presentation note. Draft at 100 items with same field mix.

final_notes:
GKR-100 final construction notes.

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers (closed-book free response, exact match after light normalisation per presentation note).

Selection criteria (all 100 items individually read with their keys):
1. Validity — excluded items with ambiguous referents (ordinal-numbered office holders, 'first PM of Congo', contested superlatives such as Romania's 3rd-highest peak), contestable premises, private/personal trivia, and items whose key did not match the wording (one item, F0130, reworded to match the key). Two wording edits in total (F0130, F0119); keys untouched.
2. Exact-match robustness — preferred keys that are a single year, full date, or single proper name; excluded keys with honorifics, trailing explanatory text, multi-entity answers, leading articles, parenthetical qualifiers, or middle initials that a correct answer would commonly omit.
3. Discrimination — the panel is results-blind, so difficulty was balanced by judgement: a minority (~15%) of moderately known anchor facts (e.g., Gauss Prize 2006, Dennis Weaver/Gunsmoke, Windows 2000, LHC 3.5 TeV) and a majority of obscure-but-citable facts (award recipients by year, exact office/death dates, founding years, episode titles). Excluded game-stat and patch-number trivia that is effectively unanswerable without retrieval and unrepresentative of general knowledge.
4. Coverage — roughly proportional to the pool with mild flattening so small fields remain represented: Science & technology 20, Politics 16, Art 12, Geography 10, Other 10, Music 9, Sports 9, History 6, TV shows 5, Video games 3. Within fields, items span regions (South Asia, Africa, Latin America, Europe, North America) and eras.

Scoring: plain accuracy, unweighted (no empirical basis for weights under the results-blind policy). Three panel runs archived (R1 86-item draft, R2 and R3 100-item drafts) for post-hoc item analysis.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. Instruct systems to answer with only the requested entity/value (name, year, or full date as requested) and no extra text. Grader should normalise trivial surface differences (case, trailing punctuation, leading/trailing whitespace, 'the' articles) before exact matching; dates should be accepted in any unambiguous day-month-year ordering matching the key.

[round 1] GKR-100 construction record.

Construct: retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge, short free-response, single dated/citable answer (SimpleQA-style). Graded by exact match against fixed human-verified key.

Round 1 decisions:
- Selection criteria applied when scanning the pool: (a) question must fully specify the target entity and the answer granularity (e.g. "day, month, and year"), (b) key must be a single unambiguous short string, (c) no first-person/context-dependent framing ("my Sigma DP1", "my maximum shutter speed"), (d) no vague quantifications of a career/period ("how many years was X's career"), (e) exclude near-universal trivia (e.g. "Who gave the slogan Quit India?", "In whose memory was the Taj Mahal built?") which cannot discriminate, (f) avoid template duplication (pool has ~10 near-identical "What year was the municipality of X, Colombia, founded?" items; kept 1).
- Coverage rationale: roughly proportional to pool composition but floored so every field is represented and no field dominates. Draft mix: Science&tech 18, Politics 14, Art 12, Geography 12, Music 10, Other 9, History 8, Sports 8, TV 5, Video games 4. Science&tech and Politics are the largest pool strata and the most practically relevant to our deployment domains, so they keep the largest shares; Video games/TV are capped because their pool items are heavily concentrated in a few franchises (Dark Souls/Terraria patch notes), which would narrow the construct.
- Panel check (round 1): accuracy spread 32.2%-64.8% across 13 systems, no ceiling/floor effects -> the set already separates capability levels.
[round 1 summary] Built initial 100-item draft with field quotas and validity screening; panel spread 32-65%.

[round 2] Round 2: item-level validity audit. Viewed all 100 draft items' full text + keys.
Removed 6 for key/wording defects rather than for difficulty:
- F0024 (SWV song; key "Right Here (Human Nature Remix)" is a remix title that exact-match grading would penalise for the canonical title).
- F0035 (David Sayer: at least two English cricketers of that name; question does not disambiguate).
- F0130 (asks "passengers" but key 583 is total fatalities incl. crew - question/key mismatch).
- F0118 ("ancient name of Orak Island" - several islands named Orak; underspecified).
- F0202 ("the vampire" in Penny Dreadful S1 - more than one referent).
- F0125 (Cindy Sherman 2001 book - multiple publications that year; key not uniquely cued).
Replacements chosen in the same fields to preserve the quota mix: F0320 (Art), F0283 (Geography), F0092 (History), F0470 (TV), F0040 (Sports), F0327 (Music). F0271 was considered but rejected: its key is a loose descriptive phrase ("Pacific Coast intercollegiate competition") that exact matching would score unreliably.
Edit (1): F0094 asked for "month and year" while the verified key is a full date; question reworded to request day, month, and year. Key untouched.
Panel after changes: 33.8%-66.2%; ordering stable vs round 1, top cluster still tight (5 systems within 2.2 pts).
[round 2 summary] Audited all items; removed 6 defective keys/ambiguous items, replaced in-field; one granularity edit. Panel 34-66%.

[round 3] Round 3: difficulty calibration.
Replaced 6 items whose answers are micro-facts about low-notability entities (exact birth/death dates of minor figures: F0245, F0137, F0329; domain-registration date F0285; obscure listing/opening dates F0192, F0228). Such items tend to be near-zero for every system (no retrievable trace), i.e. they add variance but little discrimination.
Replacements are mid-difficulty, well-documented facts about notable entities, in the same fields to preserve the quota mix: F0527 (Music), F0409 (Sports), F0507 (Art), F0382 (Sci&tech), F0430 + F0599 (Geography).
Effect on panel: all systems rose ~3-5 pts (top 70.4%, bottom 38.8%), rank order essentially unchanged, overall spread preserved (~32 pts) with less floor compression at the bottom - i.e. the same discrimination with fewer dead items.
Scoring: keeping plain accuracy with uniform weights. Field representativeness is already encoded in the quota design; adding weights on top would double-count field choices and make the score harder to interpret for model selection.
[round 3 summary] Swapped 6 non-discriminative micro-fact items for mid-difficulty notable-entity items; panel 38.8-70.4%, spread preserved.
final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge (single, dated, citable short answers), graded by exact match against fixed human-verified keys.

COVERAGE (chosen, not equal quotas): Science & technology 18, Politics 14, Art 12, Geography 12, Music 10, Other 9, History 8, Sports 8, TV shows 5, Video games 4. Shares track pool composition (the two largest strata, Sci&tech and Politics, are also the most relevant to our deployment domains) while flooring every field so the construct stays broad. TV and Video games are deliberately capped: their pool items cluster heavily in a few franchises (Dark Souls / Terraria / WoW patch notes) and over-sampling them would narrow the construct to one knowledge niche. Within fields, duplicated templates were avoided (e.g. the ~10 near-identical "year municipality X in Colombia was founded" items contribute only one).

VALIDITY SCREEN: every selected item was read in full with its key. Excluded: context-dependent or first-person framings ("my Sigma DP1"), vague quantifications of careers/periods, questions whose referent is not uniquely specified (two cricketers named David Sayer; "the vampire" in Penny Dreadful S1; "Orak Island"), question/key mismatches (passengers vs. total fatalities), keys that are loose descriptive phrases or non-canonical titles that exact matching would mis-score, and near-universal trivia that cannot discriminate (Quit India slogan, Taj Mahal). One wording edit only (F0094: granularity of the asked date aligned to the key; key untouched).

DISCRIMINATION: mid-difficulty, well-documented facts about notable entities were preferred over micro-facts on low-notability entities (exact birth/death dates of minor figures, domain-registration dates), which score near zero for all systems and add noise rather than signal. Final panel run: 38.8%-70.4% across 13 systems, no ceiling or floor effects, monotone separation of the known capability tiers (top cluster 67.6-70.4, mid 54.7-59.5, lower 38.8-44.9). Residual limitation: the top five systems sit within ~3 points, so GKR-100 separates tiers reliably but is not a fine-grained discriminator at the frontier; pair with a harder set for frontier comparisons.

SCORING: plain accuracy, uniform weights (field emphasis is already expressed through the quota design); 5 samples per item; presentation/grading conventions recorded in the format note.
presentation_note: Free-response, zero-shot, no tools/retrieval. Systems must output only the short answer string in the requested granularity (e.g. "day, month, and year" -> full date). Graded by exact match against the fixed human-verified key, normalising case, surrounding whitespace/punctuation, date format, and diacritics; no partial credit. 5 samples per item, item score = mean over samples. Uniform item weights.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Selection criteria: every item in the final set was read in full (question + key). Items were excluded if (a) the question was ambiguous or underspecified (e.g., 'the vampire' in a series with several; 'Hall Medal' with multiple namesakes), (b) the key conflicted with the question (passengers vs. total fatalities; key gives a day when the question asks month/year), (c) the key's exact-match form was an unreasonable hazard (four-part full names, honorifics, remix parentheticals), or (d) the item was common knowledge likely trivial for all systems. One wording edit (F0276, Munch 'The Day After') for clarity; keys untouched.

Field coverage (final): Science & technology 20, Politics 18, Art 13, Music 10, Geography 9, Other 9, Sports 9, History 5, TV shows 5, Video games 2. Rationale: roughly proportional to pool size, capped so no field exceeds 20%; History held at 5 because its pool is small (80); Video games held at 2 because most pool items are patch-note/stat minutiae of low general value; TV held at 5 for the same reason. Within fields, items favour prizes/awards, office-holding dates, founding/opening dates, and named discoveries—facts with a single canonical citable source.

Discrimination evidence: the full draft was run on the 13-model panel four times across rounds; final spread 36.4%-70.2% with a stable ordering (top cluster MDL-02/04/01/06, bottom cluster MDL-10/05/08/12/13). Sub-block probes (Sci+Pol, Art, Geo, Geo+Other, entertainment block) each independently reproduced the same model ordering, so no field acts as noise; 'Other' is hardest (~20-55%), Art and entertainment easiest at the top. No ceiling or floor effects.

Scoring: plain accuracy, uniform weights (no per-item panel data available to justify differential weights; difficulty is already spread across the item mix). Presentation note specifies answer-only responses and date granularity to limit format-induced exact-match failures.
presentation_note: Free-response, one item per prompt. Instruct systems to answer with only the requested value (name, year, date, number, or title) and no explanation. Dates should be given in the granularity the question asks (day/month/year, month/year, or year). Grading is exact match against the fixed key after normalization of case, punctuation, and surrounding whitespace.

notes: [round 1] Round 1 initial design: built a 100-item free-response draft covering all 10 fields. Target mix: Science/technology 18, Politics 16, Art 12, Geography 10, Other 10, Music 9, Sports 9, TV shows 6, History 5, Video games 5. Rationale: keep broad coverage while reflecting the pool's heavier science/politics/art representation; include smaller categories enough to test cross-domain retrieval but not force weak/overly niche quotas. [round 2] Round 2 validation pass: replaced 14 initially selected items with clearer alternatives. final_notes:
GKR-100 final benchmark: 100 free-response retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge items with single short answers. Scoring rule is unweighted accuracy; no item weights are used.

Coverage: Art 12, Geography 10, History 5, Music 9, Other 10, Politics 16, Science and technology 18, Sports 9, TV shows 6, Video games 5. This mix intentionally covers all ten pool fields while reflecting the pool's greater depth in science/technology, politics, and art. Smaller categories (history, TV, video games) are still represented enough to test cross-domain breadth without forcing weak or overly repetitive quotas.

Selection criteria: selected items ask for dated/citable facts such as names, years, dates, counts, awards, locations, titles, and institutions. I prioritized questions with a single unambiguous answer and a concise verified key, and avoided or removed items with common-knowledge triviality, highly free-form quote answers, malformed/space-padded keys, honorific-dependent answers, and wording that conflicted with the fixed answer format. Several prompts were lightly edited only to clarify expected date/full-name responses while leaving keys unchanged.

Discrimination: standard-panel runs after cleanup showed a broad model spread (roughly mid-20s/low-30s to mid/high-60s accuracy), indicating moderate difficulty and useful separation across system capability levels. The final set balances easier retrievable facts with specialized long-tail factual queries rather than relying on either trivial recall or obscure/unanswerable items.
presentation_note: Free-response factual questions; answers should be concise and use the requested name/date/number format when specified. Items are unweighted in round 1 pending panel difficulty review.

notes:
[round 1] Round 1 Initial Assessment & Design Strategy:
1. Construct: Retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers across 10 fields.
2. Pool analysis: 2,000 items distributed across Science and technology (413), Politics (351), Art (267), Other (213), Geography (204), Sports (157), Music (155), TV shows (108), History (80), and Video games (52).
3. Quality & Validity checks:
   - Several items in the pool suffer from answer-key formatting anomalies (e.g. trailing periods like "Barack Obama.", honorific prefixes like "Shri", overly specific long strings, or ambiguous multi-part dates like "May 16, 2015" vs "16 May 2015").
   - Under exact matching, such key anomalies cause unfair false-negative errors.
   - We must screen candidates thoroughly to select items with precise, unambiguous questions and clean, standardized keys (e.g., exact years, clean single proper names, standard numbers, concise titles).
4. Discriminative capability: Avoid items that are universally known trivia (100% across all models) or impossible noise (0% across all models). Aim for a balanced difficulty curve that spreads models across capability tiers.
5. Field coverage plan: We will target representative coverage spanning all 10 fields, roughly aligned with pool proportions with adequate sample sizes per field.

[round 2] Round 2 Evaluation & Benchmark Assembly:
1. Benchmark Configuration:
   - Full 100-item draft assembled across all 10 domain categories:
     * Science and technology: 18 items (18%)
     * Politics: 16 items (16%)
     * Art: 12 items (12%)
     * Geography: 12 items (12%)
     * History: 8 items (8%)
     * Sports: 8 items (8%)
     * Music: 8 items (8%)
     * Other: 8 items (8%)
     * TV shows: 5 items (5%)
     * Video games: 5 items (5%)
   - Construct alignment: Every item is an objective, retrieval-verifiable factual question with a single, dated/citable answer key.
   - Stringency against formatting noise: Items were rigorously audited to exclude problematic answer keys (such as trailing periods, honorific affixes, leading/trailing whitespace, or ambiguous date formatting) that could otherwise generate false negatives under exact matching.

2. Panel Results & Discrimination Analysis:
   - Panel performance spans from 18.1% (GPT-6 Luna) to 70.6% (Grok 4.7), giving a 52.5 percentage point dynamic range.
   - Clear stratification across four distinct model tiers:

final_notes:
# Project GKR-100: Benchmark Construction and Validation Report

## 1. Construct Definition & Scope
Project GKR-100 assesses model capabilities on retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge requiring single, dated, citable answers. The construct targets exact factual precision across diverse human knowledge domains rather than open-ended reasoning or subjective synthesis. Grading is conducted via exact matching against ground-truth keys.

## 2. Selection Criteria & Quality Control
Each of the 100 benchmark items was evaluated under rigorous psychometric and validity standards:
- **Construct Validity & Unambiguity**: Questions specify unambiguous target referents (exact years, named entities, proper titles, or verified quantities). Items requiring vague descriptions or multi-clause interpretations were systematically excluded.
- **Answer Key Integrity**: Pool items were scrutinized for grading noise. Items with extraneous whitespace, trailing punctuation, non-standard diacritics, honorific prefixes, or ambiguous date formats (e.g., month-day-year variations) were removed to prevent false negatives under exact matching.
- **Discriminative Sensitivity**: The set was tested empirically against the 12-model panel to ensure monotonic separation across model capability tiers. Items avoid floor effects (entry models score ~19-20%) and ceiling effects (frontier models score ~71%, providing headroom for subsequent model evaluations).

## 3. Domain Coverage & Representativeness Rationale
The 100 items represent all 10 fields in the item pool, reflecting pool density while maintaining a minimum of 5 items per category:
- **Science and Technology (18 items, 18%)**: Significant scientific milestones, computing history, formal prizes, physical constants, and aerospace engineering.
- **Politics (16 items, 16%)**: Governance, international diplomacy, judicial appointments, electoral history, and key political figures.
- **Art (12 items, 12%)**: Art history, architectural landmarks, major exhibitions, sculpture, and design chronologies.
- **Geography (12 items, 12%)**: Topography, hydrography, historical settlements, and geographic trivia.
- **History (8 items, 8%)**: Landmark treaties, historical battles, administrative milestones, and foundational figures.
- **Music (8 items, 8%)**: Chart achievements, organology, classical compositions, and contemporary music history.
- **Sports (8 items, 8%)**: Olympic chronologies, championship records, institutional leadership, and statistical facts.
- **Other (8 items, 8%)**: Academic honors, cultural artifacts, and niche domain achievements.
- **TV Shows (5 items, 5%)**: Emmy-recognized broadcasts, production history, and recurring character trivia.
- **Video Games (5 items, 5%)**: Technical patch versions, mechanical gameplay stats, and voice casting.

## 4. Scoring Configuration & Empirical Panel Results
- **Scoring Rule**: Standard accuracy (uniform 1.0 weight per item).
- **Dynamic Range**: 52.5 percentage points (18.9% to 71.4%).
- **Model Stratification**:
  * Frontier Tier: Grok 4.7 (71.4%), Claude Fable 5.1 (69.8%), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (68.5%), GPT-6.1 Sol (67.0%)
  * Advanced Tier: Gemini 4 Argon (62.0%), Gemini 3.1 Pro (51.3%)
  * Mid Tier: Grok 4.5 (46.9%), Claude Opus 5 (46.1%)
  * Entry Tier: Grok 4.3 (31.3%), GPT-5.5 (28.1%), Gemini 3.8 Flash (20.2%), GPT-6 Luna (18.9%)
presentation_note: Standard free-response exact-match evaluation for factual retrieval knowledge. Each item carries equal weight, producing an unweighted accuracy score out of 100%.

Review complete prompts and fixed keys before selection. Use uniform item weights; panel diagnostics inform difficulty and ambiguity review, not preference for any named system. final_notes: GKR-100 final: exactly 100 free-response items, uniform weight 1.0, accuracy scoring. Coverage: Art 12; Geography 12; History 10; Music 10; Other 8; Politics 14; Science and technology 16; Sports 8; TV shows 5; Video games 5. This deliberately moderates the source pool's politics/science concentration, preserves substantial coverage of those broad fields, and includes cultural, geographic, historical and entertainment knowledge. It is a balanced internal screening design, not a representative probability sample of all factual knowledge. Within fields, selection includes dated historical/institutional milestones, named works and creators, physical places and geographic events, taxonomic attribution, software/spaceflight milestones, sports results and media-release facts. All retained full prompts and fixed keys were inspected. Across four rounds, later pool positions were examined, uncertain premises and ambiguous current/first/ordinal questions were excluded, repeated award/biographical templates reduced, and wording anchored to particular events, editions, seasons, versions and time zones where necessary. Three final replacements removed an imprecise library-role premise, a partially answer-leaking planet question and a multi-person answer. Eleven edit operations were used; keys were never changed. Selection favored uniquely identifiable, retrieval-checkable factual answers and avoided speculative, subjective, overly trivial or questionable-key questions. No model-specific weights or selection objective was used. Final standard panel, five samples per item: aggregate accuracies 45.5–82.1%, indicating useful overall capability separation without benchmark-level saturation. Only aggregate results were exposed; individual-item discrimination, universal easy/hard items, significance of near-tied ranks and generalization to held-out systems are not established. Platform exact matching and immutable aliases can penalize correct alternative spellings, honorifics, translated titles, punctuation or date formats; instructions mitigate but do not eliminate this known validity limitation. The pool's human-verified retrieval keys are the source-verification basis: tools did not provide source documents or citation URLs, and no independent external citation verification is claimed. Preserve the frozen set, use complementary held-out evaluation for consequential model selection, and audit exact-match misses and source evidence before treating small score differences as knowledge differences. All four rounds' detailed construction decisions are saved in the notes.
presentation_note: GKR-100: 100 free-response factual questions, equally weighted. Return only the requested name, title, number, or date; no explanation, source quotation, or alternatives. Use the specified event date, release, edition, season or version rather than current facts. Give names/titles in their conventional English form unless the prompt specifies otherwise; include a full name where requested. For dates provide only the requested components and follow any item-specific convention. The platform uses fixed exact-match keys. It does not expose editable aliases; spelling, honorifics, punctuation and date-format variants may be scored as incorrect. This is a known grading limitation, not evidence of a factual error. Citation anchors in prompts support retrieval; the tool does not expose source URLs.

final_notes:
GKR-100: 100 free-response items measuring retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge with single, dated, citable answers.

Selection criteria: (1) Validity — every item's full text and key was read; items were excluded for ambiguous referents, contested facts, ordinal-counting ambiguity, answers embedded in the question, fictional-lore (non-dated) content, or keys with exact-match hazards (honorifics, parentheticals, unit words, inconsistent date formats). Four wording edits only (acronym expansion, fact-accurate rephrasing of F0187, and explicit date-format hints on the two US-format date keys). (2) Discrimination — panel results are aggregate-only; the full draft spreads systems from ~33% to ~66% with stable rank ordering across rounds, and block-ablation probes in Round 2 showed every field block discriminates (no block at ceiling or floor; Politics/History easiest at ~72% for top systems, Sci&Tech hardest at ~13% for the weakest). (3) Representativeness — field quotas follow pool size, adjusted for construct fit: Sci&Tech 18, Politics 15, Art 14, Geography 10, History 10, Music 9, Other 7, Sports 6, TV 6, Video games 5. Video games is capped because most pool items are game-stat wiki trivia rather than dated events; History is slightly above pool share because its items are among the cleanest dated facts.

Scoring: unweighted accuracy (no per-item panel data to justify differential weights). Presentation note specifies answer-only output, default 'D Month YYYY' date format, and light grader normalization (case, whitespace, trailing punctuation, diacritics, title quotes).

Conflict-of-interest flag: Claude Fable 5.1 (the model constructing this set) is on the panel and finishes 1st-2nd within 0.2-1 pt of Grok 4.7. All selection decisions were made on the stated validity/construct criteria and recorded in the notes; no item was chosen or dropped based on which system it favored. Reviewers may wish to spot-check this.
presentation_note: Free-response, closed-book. Systems must output only the short answer (name / year / date / title), no explanation. Dates: use "D Month YYYY" unless the question specifies otherwise; month-year items as "Month YYYY". Grader should apply light normalization before exact match: case, surrounding whitespace, trailing punctuation, diacritics, and quotation marks around titles. Unweighted accuracy over 100 items.

final_notes:
GKR-100 is a 100-item free-response set of retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge. Every item has a single human-verified short answer (a name, year, date, place, title, or count) that can be checked against a citable source. Selection favored dated awards, named firsts, Olympic and sports results, and specific cultural or geographic facts, and rejected items whose wording was ambiguous, whose referent was disputed, or whose key included a unit, honorific, or formatting quirk a correct answer would miss.

Coverage is uneven on purpose. Science and technology (19) is the largest slice because that pool is richest in dated, single-answer facts (medalists, discoveries, affiliations). Sports (13), art (11), geography (10), history (10), and music (10) carry the mid-range. Politics (7) and Other (7) are smaller because those pools are heavy on obscure personal dates. TV shows (9) and video games (4) are included so the set is not only academic, but video games is capped: the pool is small (52) and much of it is patch-number trivia that does not separate general capability. Equal quotas were rejected; the mix tracks where clean, citable items actually exist.

Discriminative design. Near-universal facts (Taj Mahal, Austerlitz, Handel, the cricket World Cup triple) are kept as anchors but weighted 0.5. Specialized but still citable facts (Eckert–Mauchly, Kanellakis, Riemann Prize, Stampacchia, SIGPLAN dissertation award, Hall Medal) are weighted 1.25–1.5. Everything else is 1.0. Scoring is weighted_accuracy so common knowledge does not dominate the ranking. Fourteen questions were rewritten only to pin answer form (date order, single word, country or city name only); keys were never changed. Items dropped across rounds include disputed attributions (Quit India slogan), unstable counts (Tenerife deaths, lightning odds), underspecified referents, and keys that exact-match cannot fairly grade.

Presentation: answer with the shortest form the question asks for, no titles of address, dates in the order requested. The set is for internal model selection on retrieval-verifiable factual knowledge, not reasoning or generation quality.

Item weights down-weight widely known facts and up-weight specialized but still citable facts so the score separates capability levels.
